title: Fourth-generation allosteric inhibitors for on-target escape from osimertinib in EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Third-generation covalent inhibitors, principally osimertinib, are now standard therapy for advanced lung adenocarcinoma driven by activating EGFR alleles, yet nearly every tumor progresses within two to three years. In roughly 7 to 15 percent of progressions the driver is a tertiary substitution, C797S, that removes the nucleophilic cysteine required for covalent engagement and abolishes activity of every approved irreversible agent. Whether C797S is acquired on the same allele as the T790M gatekeeper or on the reciprocal allele determines whether any existing regimen retains activity, and this configuration is almost never resolved by standard short-read panels reported in clinical practice. We will define the allelic architecture of tertiary EGFR alleles across a 400-patient progression cohort using long-read phasing, advance allosteric inhibitors that engage a pocket distinct from the ATP site and therefore do not require Cys797, and test rationally paired regimens in models established directly from progressing patients.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Determine the frequency and allelic phase of tertiary EGFR substitutions at progression. We will apply targeted long-read sequencing to 400 paired pre-treatment and progression specimens, resolving cis versus trans configuration of C797S relative to T790M and to the L858R or exon 19 deletion driver, and relate configuration to subsequent treatment benefit. Aim 2. Optimize allosteric EGFR inhibitors active against triple-mutant receptors. Starting from the EAI045 chemotype, we will iterate analogs guided by co-crystallography and biochemical selectivity panels, targeting cellular IC50 below 25 nM against L858R/T790M/C797S with at least 40-fold sparing of the wild-type receptor. Aim 3. Define regimens that suppress the emergence of escape. We will test allosteric agents alone and paired with cetuximab or with a MEK inhibitor in models grown from progression biopsies, using continuous dosing to measure time to regrowth rather than tumor shrinkage alone.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Patients whose disease progresses on osimertinib have no approved targeted option. Chemotherapy remains the default, with median progression-free survival of roughly 4.4 months and substantial toxicity. Among mechanisms that are in principle druggable, tertiary substitution of Cys797 is the single most common, and unlike heterogeneous downstream events it leaves the tumor entirely dependent on the same receptor. The therapeutic problem is therefore not target identification but chemistry: every marketed agent for this receptor either requires the mutated cysteine for covalent attachment or is blocked by the gatekeeper methionine. Solving this yields a regimen applicable to several thousand patients annually in the United States alone, and provides a template for on-target escape in other covalently drugged kinases including BTK and KRAS. The allelic phasing work will additionally change how progression specimens are reported, since cis and trans configurations imply opposite clinical decisions.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: Three elements are new. First, we treat allelic phase as a therapeutic variable rather than a sequencing curiosity; no prior study has systematically phased tertiary EGFR alleles at scale, because short-read panels collapse reads shorter than the 500 base pairs separating codons 790 and 797. Second, our chemistry does not compete with ATP. Compounds occupying the pocket vacated when the regulatory helix shifts inward are insensitive to the steric bulk of the gatekeeper and do not depend on Cys797, inverting the usual liability of the mutant receptor into a selectivity handle. Third, we score candidate regimens by time to regrowth under uninterrupted dosing in models carrying the patient alleles, rather than by maximal regression, because durability rather than depth of response is the unmet need. Together these shift the field from cataloguing escape events to preventing them.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Progression specimens and matched pre-treatment tissue will be accrued from three institutions under an existing protocol; adaptive sampling on a nanopore platform will enrich the EGFR locus to a mean depth of 800-fold, sufficient to phase variants at 2 percent allele fraction. Analog synthesis will proceed in iterative cycles of eight to twelve compounds, with biochemical potency measured against a panel of nine recombinant EGFR constructs and cellular activity in Ba/F3 lines and in models grown from patient tumors. Co-crystals of lead compounds with the L858R/T790M/C797S kinase domain will be solved to 2.1 angstrom or better to guide substitution at the aniline and pyrimidine vectors. In vivo efficacy will use subcutaneous and orthotopic implants from six donors, dosed to steady state and followed to regrowth, with tumors at regrowth resequenced to identify the next escape event. Statistical power calculations assume a two-fold difference in time to regrowth with eight animals per arm.

title: MET-driven bypass signaling and combined MET plus EGFR blockade in EGFR-mutant lung cancer

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Focal amplification of the MET receptor is the most common driver-independent route by which EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma escapes osimertinib, detected in 15 to 20 percent of progression specimens after first-line therapy. Amplified MET restores phosphorylation of ERBB3 and thereby reactivates PI3K and ERK output while EGFR remains fully inhibited, which explains why single-agent MET inhibitors fail and why concurrent suppression of both receptors is required. Progress has been slowed by disagreement about what constitutes a therapeutically meaningful degree of amplification, with trials variously requiring gene copy number of 5, 6, or 10 or a MET to centromere ratio above 2. This project will establish a quantitative threshold anchored to signaling output rather than to assay convention, will define the determinants of depth and duration of response to paired receptor blockade, and will characterize what emerges when the paired regimen itself fails.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Anchor amplification thresholds to biology. Across 250 progression specimens profiled by sequencing, fluorescence in situ hybridization, and immunohistochemistry, we will relate copy gain to receptor phosphorylation and to downstream ERK and AKT activity in the same tissue, and identify the copy number at which the tumor becomes dependent on the second receptor. Aim 2. Define response determinants for dual receptor blockade. Using tumors grown from 30 donors, we will test osimertinib together with savolitinib or tepotinib and ask whether co-occurring alterations in TP53, RB1, PIK3CA, or CDKN2A blunt response. Aim 3. Characterize escape from dual blockade. Serial specimens from patients treated on NCT03778229 and from long-term treated models will be profiled to determine whether escape proceeds through secondary kinase-domain substitutions in MET such as D1228N and Y1230C, through further copy gain, or through a third receptor.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: More than a fifth of patients progressing on osimertinib have a tumor that has simply rerouted the same signal through a second receptor. This is the most tractable form of escape because the pathway remains addicted to receptor tyrosine kinase input and because inhibitors of the second receptor are already approved for other indications. Yet response rates in reported cohorts range from 30 to 66 percent, and the variance tracks almost entirely with how amplification was defined at enrollment. A threshold anchored to signaling rather than to a legacy cytogenetic convention would immediately improve patient selection and would make cross-trial comparison possible. The work also has implications beyond this receptor pair, because copy-gain-driven rerouting is a recurring theme in ALK-, ROS1-, and KRAS-driven disease, and the calibration framework developed here is directly transferable.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: We invert the usual order of biomarker development. Rather than choosing a cut point statistically from outcome data and then rationalizing it, we measure the signaling consequence of copy gain in the same tissue section and define the threshold where the second receptor becomes load-bearing. This requires multiplexed quantitative immunofluorescence for phospho-MET, phospho-ERBB3, phospho-ERK, and phospho-AKT registered to the same nuclei used for copy scoring, an assay we have already validated to a coefficient of variation below 12 percent. A second innovation is our escape-from-escape design: we deliberately treat models to regrowth on the dual regimen, because the field currently has almost no data on what follows failure of paired receptor blockade, and clinical decisions after that point are made without evidence.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Specimens derive from an institutional progression protocol and from two cooperative group trials. Copy number will be called from a 523-gene panel with orthogonal confirmation by dual-color in situ hybridization scored by two pathologists blinded to sequencing. Tumor models will be established from core biopsies and pleural fluid with an expected take rate near 40 percent; each will be genotyped and authenticated against the donor. Drug testing will use six-point dose matrices with Bliss independence scoring, and lead combinations will advance to implanted models dosed for at least 90 days. Escape lesions will undergo exome and transcriptome sequencing. For Aim 1, 250 specimens provide 85 percent power to detect a difference in phospho-ERK of 0.6 standard deviations between copy-number strata at a two-sided alpha of 0.05. All assay code and scoring rubrics will be deposited on publication.

title: Longitudinal plasma genomic surveillance of resistance emergence in oncogene-driven non-small cell lung cancer

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Escape from targeted therapy is usually detected only when a scan shows growth, by which time the responsible alteration has been expanding for months and often coexists with two or three others. Circulating tumor DNA offers a route to observe that expansion while it is still small, but the field lacks the longitudinal, densely sampled cohorts needed to establish what a rising variant actually predicts. We will enroll 600 patients starting first-line therapy for EGFR-, ALK-, ROS1-, or KRAS-driven lung adenocarcinoma and collect blood every six weeks through progression and beyond, generating an estimated 6,000 timepoints. We will determine the lead time between molecular and radiographic progression, quantify how often multiple independent escape alterations coexist, and test whether the diversity of alterations present at progression predicts benefit from the next line of therapy. A tissue substudy will calibrate what blood-based profiling systematically misses.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Quantify lead time. Using a 129-gene panel with unique molecular identifiers and a limit of detection near 0.1 percent variant allele fraction, we will measure the interval between first detection of an escape alteration and radiographic progression, powered to estimate a median lead time of 2 to 4 months with a 95 percent confidence interval narrower than 6 weeks. Aim 2. Map the architecture of escape. We will count independent alterations per progression event, phase them where depth allows, and test the hypothesis that patients whose progression involves three or more distinct alterations derive shorter benefit from subsequent targeted therapy. Aim 3. Calibrate the blind spots. In 150 patients with paired progression biopsies, we will determine how often blood misses events that tissue reveals, with particular attention to lesion states that leave little detectable in the circulation.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Every decision made at progression rests on a single biopsy of a single lesion at a single time. That sample is often taken from the most accessible rather than the most informative site, and it captures none of the trajectory that produced the lesion. Dense serial sampling changes the unit of observation from a snapshot to a curve, and curves permit questions that snapshots cannot answer: when did this alteration appear, how fast is it expanding, is it one event or four. If lead time proves substantial and reproducible, it opens the possibility of switching therapy before bulk regrowth, when the escaping population is smallest and least diverse. If diversity at progression predicts poor benefit from the next agent, it provides a rational basis for choosing broad chemotherapy over a second targeted attempt in patients whose disease has already fragmented.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: The innovation is sampling density rather than assay novelty. Existing studies collect blood at baseline and at progression, which is exactly the design that cannot measure lead time. Six-week sampling through and beyond progression, sustained across 600 patients, produces a data structure that does not currently exist for this disease. We pair it with a deliberate negative-control substudy: rather than assuming blood-based profiling is comprehensive, we quantify its failure modes against matched tissue, including cases where the biopsy shows a lesion whose morphology has changed entirely and whose alterations are inconspicuous in the circulation. Finally, all variant calls, quality metrics, and clinical annotations will be released under a data use agreement at 18 months rather than at publication, so that the cohort functions as a shared resource.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Patients will be enrolled at four sites within 30 days of starting therapy. Blood will be drawn into cell-stabilizing tubes every six weeks and at progression, processed within 6 hours, and sequenced to a median unique depth of 15,000-fold. Radiographic assessment follows RECIST 1.1 every 8 to 12 weeks by a central reader blinded to molecular results, which is essential because unblinded reading would contaminate the lead-time estimate. Progression biopsies will be requested from all patients and obtained in an anticipated 40 percent, with histologic review by a thoracic pathologist. Lead time will be modeled with interval-censored survival methods; the association between alteration count and subsequent benefit will use Cox models with alteration count as a time-fixed covariate measured at progression, adjusted for driver class, prior lines, and performance status. Target accrual is 200 patients per year for three years.

title: Lineage plasticity and neuroendocrine conversion as an escape route from EGFR inhibition

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: In 3 to 14 percent of patients whose lung adenocarcinoma progresses on EGFR-directed therapy, the repeat biopsy no longer looks like the original tumor: glandular architecture is gone, the cells are small with scant cytoplasm and molded nuclei, synaptophysin and INSM1 are positive, and the proliferative index exceeds 80 percent. The founding EGFR alteration is retained, proving descent from the original clone, but the tumor has abandoned the identity that made it drug-dependent. Antecedent biallelic loss of RB1 and TP53 is nearly universal and precedes the switch by many months. This project will define the chromatin and transcription-factor events that license conversion, determine whether the converting population is present before therapy or arises during it, and test whether the switch can be blocked or reversed pharmacologically before it becomes fixed.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Establish the temporal order of events. Using 60 longitudinal patient series with pre-treatment, on-treatment, and converted specimens, we will determine when RB1 and TP53 are lost relative to the appearance of neuroendocrine markers, and whether cells expressing ASCL1 are detectable in pre-treatment tissue by targeted in situ methods. Aim 2. Define the licensing chromatin state. We will apply single-nucleus ATAC and RNA profiling to converting tumors and to autochthonous models, testing the hypothesis that de-repression of the ASCL1 and NEUROD1 enhancer landscape requires prior loss of EZH2-dependent silencing at the alveolar identity program. Aim 3. Interrupt conversion. In models engineered to lose Rb1 and Trp53 on an Egfr-driven background, we will ask whether EZH2 inhibition, LSD1 inhibition, or Notch activation prevents or reverses the switch, using continuous erlotinib or osimertinib pressure and scoring conversion frequency at 16 weeks.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Conversion is the least tractable form of escape. Unlike a secondary kinase substitution or a second receptor, it cannot be addressed by better inhibitor chemistry, because the tumor no longer requires the receptor at all. Survival after conversion is dismal, with median overall survival under 11 months despite platinum-etoposide, and no targeted option exists. It is also almost certainly underdiagnosed, since it can only be recognized on tissue, and most progression events are worked up in blood or not at all. Establishing that RB1 and TP53 loss marks a population at risk would justify prospective re-biopsy policies in a defined subgroup rather than universally. Establishing that the switch requires a specific, druggable chromatin state would create the first opportunity to prevent an escape route rather than to chase it after the fact.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: The field has treated conversion as a categorical event observed at progression. We treat it as a trajectory with a licensing step, a commitment step, and a fixation step, each with distinct pharmacology. This requires longitudinal human material at a scale not previously assembled, and autochthonous models in which the permissive genotype is engineered but the switch remains stochastic, so that frequency becomes a measurable phenotype. We also introduce a prevention endpoint. Every prior therapeutic study has started from converted tumors, which are by then epigenetically fixed and uniformly resistant; asking instead whether an agent lowers conversion frequency under sustained receptor blockade is a different experiment with a different and more attainable success criterion.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Human specimens come from three institutional cohorts with mandated re-biopsy at progression. Central pathology review will apply defined criteria including morphology, synaptophysin, chromogranin, INSM1, and Ki-67, with discordant cases adjudicated by a third reviewer. Single-nucleus multiome profiling will target 5,000 nuclei per specimen, with regulon inference and motif enrichment used to nominate transcription factors. Mouse work uses an EgfrL858R; Rb1fl/fl; Trp53fl/fl allele set with lineage tracing from Sftpc, allowing us to prove that converted cells descend from alveolar type 2 progenitors rather than from a pre-existing neuroendocrine population. Conversion frequency will be scored blinded across at least 20 animals per arm, powered to detect a reduction from 45 percent to 15 percent with 80 percent power. Chromatin profiling of treated models will test target engagement independently of phenotype.

title: Structure-guided therapeutics for EGFR exon 20 insertion lung adenocarcinoma

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Insertions in the loop following the C-helix of EGFR account for roughly 10 percent of EGFR-altered lung adenocarcinoma and behave, pharmacologically, like a different disease. These alleles adopt an active conformation without enlarging the drug-binding cleft, so agents optimized against exon 19 deletions and L858R lose 10- to 100-fold potency while retaining full activity against the wild-type receptor, producing dose-limiting rash and diarrhea before tumor concentrations are reached. Response rates to erlotinib, gefitinib, and osimertinib are below 12 percent. Two strategies can break this constraint: compounds shaped to the narrowed pocket, and agents that do not use the pocket at all, such as dual-targeting immunoglobulins that engage the receptor ectodomain and MET simultaneously and deplete both receptors from the surface. This project pursues both, and defines what limits their durability.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Define the conformational determinants of insertion-selective binding. We will solve structures of the kinase domain bearing the four most common insertions, including V769_D770insASV, D770_N771insSVD, and H773_V774insNPH, alone and with candidate inhibitors, and relate pocket volume to measured selectivity over the wild-type receptor. Aim 2. Advance an insertion-selective chemotype to candidate status, with a target of 30-fold or greater cellular selectivity over wild type and brain exposure sufficient for intracranial activity. Aim 3. Determine why responses to receptor-depleting immunoglobulins are partial and brief. Using specimens from patients treated with amivantamab and models grown from them, we will test whether benefit is limited by incomplete receptor removal, by antibody effector cell availability, or by rapid engagement of alternative receptors, and will evaluate the addition of a pocket-directed inhibitor.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Patients with insertion alleles are routinely told they have EGFR-mutant lung cancer and then respond for three months to a drug that works for two years in their neighbors. The gap is entirely pharmacological, and it is solvable. Selectivity over the wild-type receptor is the critical variable, because it sets how much drug can be given, and therefore whether the mutant is ever meaningfully engaged in a patient rather than in a cell line. A compound with 30-fold selectivity and adequate brain exposure would convert a chemotherapy-first disease into a targeted-therapy-first disease for several thousand patients per year. Understanding the ceiling on receptor-depleting antibodies matters equally, because those agents are already approved and their benefit is currently capped near a 40 percent response rate with a median duration under a year.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: Prior medicinal chemistry in this space optimized potency against the mutant and measured selectivity as an afterthought. We treat the ratio itself as the primary optimization variable and enforce it at every cycle with a paired assay run in isogenic lines differing only at the insertion. Structurally, we characterize insertions individually rather than as a class, because a three-residue insertion after position 770 and one after position 773 produce measurably different pockets and, we predict, different selectivity ceilings. The antibody arm is innovative in asking a mechanistic rather than an empirical question: current combination trials pair agents by convenience, whereas we first determine which of three candidate limits is operative and then choose the partner accordingly.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Kinase domain constructs will be expressed in insect cells and crystallized in the presence of ligand, targeting 2.0 to 2.6 angstrom resolution; where crystals fail we will use cryo-electron microscopy of the full ectodomain-transmembrane assembly in nanodiscs. Selectivity will be measured in isogenic Ba/F3 and immortalized bronchial epithelial pairs and confirmed by receptor phosphorylation in normal human keratinocytes as a surrogate for skin toxicity. Twelve tumor models from insertion-bearing donors, including four from patients previously treated with amivantamab, will be used for efficacy and for mechanistic dissection, with natural killer cell depletion used to test the effector-cell hypothesis. Intracranial activity will be assessed in a stereotactic implantation model with quantification of unbound drug in cerebrospinal fluid. Correlative specimens from NCT04988295 will be analyzed under an existing agreement.

title: Drug-tolerant persistence in oncogene-driven lung cancer: origins, maintenance, and eradication

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Even the deepest responses to EGFR or ALK inhibition leave behind a small population of viable cells that neither die nor divide appreciably while drug is present. This reservoir is the reason responses are not cures, and it is the substrate from which every later escape event is drawn. Cells in this state are reversibly reprogrammed rather than mutated: they upregulate a diapause-like transcriptional program, become dependent on lipid peroxide detoxification through GPX4, shift chromatin toward a KDM5A-associated repressed state, and revert to full drug sensitivity when drug is withdrawn. This program project brings together three laboratories to determine where these cells come from, what keeps them alive, and whether a scheduled intervention delivered during maximal response can eliminate them before any heritable alteration is acquired.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Project 1 will determine the origin of the surviving population, using expressed barcodes to test whether survival is drawn from a pre-existing subpopulation or arises stochastically after exposure, with barcode diversity at day 14 as the discriminating readout. Project 2 will define maintenance dependencies through genome-wide screens conducted in cells already held under drug for 10 days rather than in naive cells, an ordering that we show yields a largely non-overlapping hit list dominated by lipid peroxidation defense, autophagy, and aurora kinase A. Project 3 will test scheduled eradication in vivo: after 4 weeks of continuous EGFR or ALK inhibition and confirmed maximal regression, animals will receive a GPX4 inhibitor, an aurora inhibitor, or vehicle, with time to regrowth and residual cell burden by lineage tracing as co-primary endpoints.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: The clinical shape of targeted therapy is a steep response followed by a plateau and then regrowth. The plateau is the reservoir. Every mechanistic paper on escape describes what the reservoir eventually becomes; almost none address why it survives the first two weeks. Intervening at maximal response is attractive because the cell number is at its lowest, the population has not yet diversified, and the patient is clinically well and able to tolerate a second agent. It is also testable: time to regrowth under continuous therapy is a clean preclinical endpoint and translates directly into a trial design in which a second agent is added at best response rather than at progression. If a scheduled intervention lengthens the plateau even modestly, it changes how the entire class of oncogene-directed drugs is administered.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: Three methodological commitments distinguish this program. We screen in the surviving state rather than in naive cells, which reorders the hit list entirely and explains why conventional screens have nominated targets that fail on validation. We use expressed lineage barcodes with a bottleneck design calibrated so that pre-existing and induced models predict a ten-fold difference in surviving barcode diversity, making the two hypotheses genuinely separable rather than rhetorically opposed. And we score therapy by time to regrowth under uninterrupted drug rather than by tumor shrinkage, because shrinkage is already maximal in these models and is therefore uninformative about the very population we intend to kill.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Human lines and models grown from patient tumors carrying exon 19 deletion, L858R, or EML4-ALK will be used throughout, with at least three genotypes per experiment to guard against line-specific effects. Barcode libraries of 10^6 complexity will be introduced at low multiplicity, with 500 cells per barcode maintained at the pre-treatment bottleneck. Genome-wide CRISPR screens will be performed at day 10 of continuous exposure with 500-fold library representation and two independent guide libraries. Lipid peroxidation will be quantified with C11-BODIPY, and ferroptotic death confirmed by rescue with ferrostatin-1. In vivo studies use implanted tumors from six donors, four arms, twelve animals per arm, powered to detect a doubling of time to regrowth. Residual burden during the plateau will be quantified by lineage-labeled nuclei per gram of tissue, a measurement that imaging cannot provide.

title: Sequential ALK and ROS1 inhibition: compound mutations and the limits of potency escalation

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Patients with ALK-rearranged lung cancer now receive two, three, or four kinase inhibitors in sequence, each more potent than the last. This strategy has extended median survival beyond six years but has also created a problem that did not exist when only crizotinib was available: tumors that accumulate two or three substitutions within the same kinase domain on the same allele. Compound alleles such as G1202R plus L1198F or G1202R plus L1196M are refractory to every approved agent, and their prevalence rises with each additional line of therapy, reaching roughly 35 percent of biopsies after lorlatinib. The same logic applies to ROS1, where solvent-front G2032R dominates and compound alleles are beginning to appear. This project asks whether sequencing strategy itself can be designed to avoid generating untreatable alleles.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Catalogue compound alleles and their drug sensitivity. We will genotype 300 post-progression specimens with phasing, and measure sensitivity of each recurrent compound allele to crizotinib, alectinib, brigatinib, ceritinib, lorlatinib, and two investigational agents in isogenic systems, producing a public sensitivity matrix. Aim 2. Test whether inhibitor order determines the alleles that emerge. In accelerated mutagenesis screens and in long-term treated models, we will compare lorlatinib-first with alectinib-then-lorlatinib sequences and score the spectrum and treatability of emergent alleles. Aim 3. Evaluate alternatives to further potency escalation, including a compound that binds a site distinct from the ATP cleft and a heterobifunctional molecule that removes the fusion protein rather than inhibiting it, both tested against the compound alleles defined in Aim 1.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: The prevailing strategy in this disease has been to answer each resistant allele with a more potent inhibitor. That strategy is approaching its natural limit. Once two substitutions coexist on one allele, the pocket has been remodeled in ways that no ATP-competitive chemistry has yet overcome, and each additional line of therapy raises the probability of reaching that state. If inhibitor order shapes which alleles emerge, then the sequence of therapy becomes a modifiable determinant of long-term outcome, and the current practice of choosing agents by response rate alone is inadequate. If it does not, then the field must pivot to modalities that do not depend on the pocket at all. Either answer changes practice for the roughly 5 percent of lung adenocarcinoma driven by these fusions.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: We treat therapy sequence as an experimental variable rather than as a clinical convention, which requires long-term in vivo studies of a duration rarely attempted, up to 12 months of continuous dosing with serial blood sampling. Our phasing approach resolves whether two substitutions occupy the same allele, a distinction that is clinically decisive and that standard reporting collapses. We also break with potency escalation by evaluating two orthogonal modalities in parallel against the same allele panel, so that the comparison is like-for-like. Finally, the sensitivity matrix will be released as a living resource updated as new alleles are observed, addressing a practical gap in which clinicians encounter an allele reported in fewer than five patients worldwide and have nowhere to look.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Specimens derive from an international registry of patients treated with two or more inhibitors. Phasing uses long-read sequencing of amplicons spanning the kinase domain. Isogenic Ba/F3 lines will be generated for each allele observed twice or more, with IC50 determined in triplicate across nine concentrations and reported alongside achievable unbound plasma concentrations for each drug so that sensitivity is interpreted against clinically attainable exposure. Accelerated mutagenesis uses ENU-treated cells plated at limiting dilution under each agent. In vivo sequencing studies use implanted tumors from four donors with 15 animals per sequence arm, blood sampled monthly, and progression lesions genotyped. Degrader and allosteric compounds will be profiled for selectivity across a 468-kinase panel and for brain exposure, since intracranial progression is the dominant clinical pattern in this population.

title: Adaptive and acquired escape from KRAS G12C inhibitors in lung adenocarcinoma

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Covalent inhibitors that trap KRAS G12C in its inactive state, sotorasib and adagrasib, produce objective responses in roughly 37 to 43 percent of previously treated lung adenocarcinoma but a median progression-free survival of only 6.5 months, far short of what oncogene-directed therapy achieves in EGFR- or ALK-driven disease. Two distinct problems account for the gap. Within hours of dosing, relief of ERK-dependent negative feedback restores upstream receptor signaling and reloads the target with GTP, blunting depth of response before any mutation exists. Over months, escape becomes genetic and strikingly fragmented, with individual patients acquiring four or more independent alterations including secondary KRAS substitutions, MET amplification, and fusions involving RET or ALK. This project addresses both, and asks whether suppressing the first prevents the second.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Quantify the adaptive rebound and its determinants. Using timed biopsies at 6 and 48 hours in 40 patients and matched models, we will measure target occupancy, GTP loading, and ERK output, and test whether the magnitude of rebound at 48 hours predicts depth of radiographic response. Aim 2. Determine whether blocking the rebound deepens and prolongs response. We will pair G12C inhibitors with SHP2 or SOS1 inhibitors and with anti-EGFR antibodies in models from 20 donors, scoring depth of regression and time to regrowth. Aim 3. Map acquired escape and its fragmentation. Serial blood and progression biopsies from 120 patients will be profiled to count independent alterations per patient and to test the hypothesis that regimens producing deeper initial responses yield fewer simultaneous escape events.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: KRAS G12C is present in roughly 13 percent of lung adenocarcinoma, making it more common than ALK, ROS1, RET, and exon 20 insertions combined. The first generation of inhibitors proved the target is druggable but delivered a fraction of the benefit seen with other oncogene-directed agents, and the reason is now reasonably clear: the target is not silenced but merely slowed, and the cell restores signaling faster than the drug can accumulate. Whether the correct response is more potent covalent chemistry, agents that also engage the active state, or upstream co-suppression is an open and consequential question. The fragmentation of acquired escape has a second implication: if a typical patient progresses with four independent alterations, then sequential single-agent salvage is unlikely ever to work in this disease, and trial design should reflect that.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: The 6-hour and 48-hour biopsy schedule is unusual and deliberate; it captures the rebound in patients rather than inferring it from cell lines, and it makes the pharmacodynamic rebound a measurable clinical covariate. We also test a specific and falsifiable link between the two halves of the problem, namely that deeper suppression early produces less diverse escape later, by comparing alteration counts at progression across regimens with differing depth of response. This connects short-term pharmacology to long-term evolutionary outcome, a link usually asserted but rarely measured. Finally, we include patients progressing on these agents in an obligate re-biopsy protocol, giving the first systematic tissue view of escape rather than a blood-only view that under-detects copy gain and fusions.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Clinical specimens come from three trials and an institutional protocol. Target occupancy will be measured by mass spectrometry of the tryptic peptide containing the modified cysteine, and GTP loading by RBD pulldown normalized to total protein. Response depth will be quantified as percentage change in sum of target lesion diameters, analyzed as a continuous variable against 48-hour ERK output using linear regression with 40 patients providing 80 percent power to detect a correlation coefficient of 0.45. Combination studies use six-by-six dose matrices and implanted models dosed to regrowth, with 10 animals per arm. Progression material will undergo exome, transcriptome, and fusion-capture sequencing; alteration counts will be compared across regimens with negative binomial regression adjusted for duration of therapy.

title: Central nervous system pharmacology of next-generation lung cancer kinase inhibitors

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Roughly 40 percent of patients with EGFR-mutant and 50 percent with ALK-rearranged lung adenocarcinoma develop intracranial disease, and in the modern era the neuraxis is frequently the first and sometimes the only site of progression. Whether an agent controls that compartment depends on unbound concentration achieved beyond the neurovascular barrier, which is governed by efflux at the endothelium, principally by ABCB1 and ABCG2, and by plasma protein binding. Reported ratios for this drug class span three orders of magnitude and are frequently measured as total rather than unbound drug, rendering them uninterpretable. This project will generate a rigorous, cross-comparable dataset of unbound partitioning for twelve agents, determine how efflux transporter polymorphisms and prior radiotherapy modify it, and test whether transporter inhibition or structural modification can raise partitioning enough to matter clinically.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Measure unbound partitioning rigorously for twelve agents including osimertinib, lazertinib, alectinib, brigatinib, lorlatinib, entrectinib, repotrectinib, sotorasib, and adagrasib, using microdialysis in tumor-bearing animals and equilibrium dialysis to correct for binding, with partitioning reported as unbound tissue to unbound plasma ratio. Aim 2. Determine the contribution of efflux. Using Abcb1 and Abcg2 knockout animals and a transporter inhibitor, we will quantify how much of the observed gradient each transporter explains, and relate this to intracranial efficacy in stereotactic implantation models. Aim 3. Translate to patients. In 80 patients undergoing lumbar puncture or ventricular sampling for clinical indications, we will measure unbound drug concentrations and relate them to intracranial response, genotype at ABCB1, and prior cranial irradiation.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: Intracranial control has become the dominant determinant of quality of life and often of survival in oncogene-driven lung cancer, because systemic disease is well controlled for years. Drug selection for this compartment is currently made from anecdote and from small trial subsets, and the underlying pharmacology is documented inconsistently. A single, internally consistent dataset comparing twelve agents under identical conditions would immediately inform sequencing decisions, and the transporter work would explain why structurally similar compounds differ ten-fold. The clinical arm addresses a question that animals cannot: whether prior radiotherapy durably alters barrier integrity, which matters because a large fraction of patients have received it and are then assumed to have the same pharmacology as those who have not.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: Unbound rather than total measurement is the central methodological commitment, and it is not merely technical: for highly bound compounds such as lorlatinib the two differ by more than 30-fold and rank agents in a different order. Microdialysis in tumor-bearing rather than naive animals is a second departure, since tumor tissue disrupts the barrier locally and naive measurements systematically understate reachable concentrations. The knockout and inhibitor arms allow attribution of the gradient to specific transporters instead of treating penetration as an unexplained compound property. Finally, we prospectively collect cerebrospinal fluid at defined times relative to dosing rather than opportunistically, so that the human data can be modeled rather than merely tabulated.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Microdialysis probes will be placed in tumor-bearing and contralateral normal tissue, with sampling over 24 hours at steady state and recovery determined by retrodialysis. Equilibrium dialysis will determine unbound fraction in plasma and tissue homogenate. Efficacy studies use luciferase-labeled implants from four donors with bioluminescent tracking twice weekly and survival as the endpoint, 12 animals per arm. Human sampling will be timed to 2, 6, and 24 hours post-dose where feasible, with paired blood; assay sensitivity is 0.1 ng/mL by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Association between measured concentration and intracranial response will be modeled with logistic regression adjusted for prior radiotherapy and lesion size; 80 patients provide 80 percent power to detect an odds ratio of 3.0 per log-unit increase in concentration.

title: Antibody-drug conjugates and the immune contexture of EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: After progression on osimertinib, roughly half of patients have no identifiable targetable alteration, and for them the only options are platinum doublets and, increasingly, agents that deliver a cytotoxic payload to a surface antigen. HER3 is expressed on more than 80 percent of EGFR-mutant tumors regardless of the mechanism of progression, making it an attractive address, and patritumab deruxtecan produces responses in roughly 30 percent of heavily pretreated patients independent of how they escaped osimertinib. What determines that response is unknown: antigen density, internalization rate, payload sensitivity, and the surrounding immune contexture are all plausible and rarely measured together. This project will determine what predicts benefit, will characterize the immunologically inert state characteristic of these tumors, and will test whether payload-induced immunogenic cell death can be leveraged to make checkpoint blockade work in a population where it reliably does not.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Identify determinants of response to HER3-directed payload delivery. In 130 patients treated on two trials, we will quantify antigen density by mass cytometry-calibrated immunohistochemistry, internalization in matched models, and SLFN11 expression as a determinant of topoisomerase I payload sensitivity, and relate each to response. Aim 2. Characterize the immune contexture. Using imaging mass cytometry on 200 specimens, we will quantify CD8 T-cell density and spatial distribution, macrophage polarization, and antigen presentation machinery, comparing EGFR-mutant with EGFR-wild-type tumors. Aim 3. Test whether payload-induced cell death converts the contexture. In immunocompetent models bearing Egfr-driven tumors, we will combine payload delivery with PD-1 blockade and measure T-cell priming, clonal expansion of tumor-reactive receptors, and survival.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: The post-osimertinib setting is now the largest unmet need in EGFR-mutant lung cancer, encompassing approximately 15,000 patients per year in the United States. Payload-delivering agents are the first class in a decade to show meaningful activity there, but with a 30 percent response rate and a median duration near 7 months, unselected use wastes both drug and time. A validated selection strategy would roughly double the benefit per patient treated. Separately, the failure of checkpoint blockade in this population is well documented and poorly explained; response rates below 10 percent are consistently reported despite the fact that these tumors are not uniformly devoid of T cells. Determining whether the barrier is exclusion, exhaustion, or antigen presentation would settle a decade-long controversy and guide whether combination strategies are worth pursuing at all.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: We measure the three candidate determinants of payload benefit in the same patients rather than separately across studies, which is the only way to establish which dominates. Calibrated antigen quantification replaces the ordinal scoring that has repeatedly failed to predict benefit for this class of agent. On the immune side, spatial single-cell imaging lets us distinguish exclusion from exhaustion, two states that bulk expression signatures conflate and that imply opposite interventions. The immunocompetent modeling is also unusual for this disease, since most EGFR-driven models are grown in animals lacking adaptive immunity, which forecloses the very question we are asking.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Trial specimens are available under existing agreements from NCT04619004 and an investigator-initiated study. Antigen density will be reported as receptors per cell using calibration beads, with a pre-specified threshold of 20,000 receptors per cell tested against response by logistic regression; 130 patients provide 80 percent power to detect an odds ratio of 2.8. Imaging mass cytometry will use a 36-marker panel with neighborhood analysis to define cellular niches. Mouse studies use an inducible EgfrL858R model on a C57BL/6 background crossed to a human HER3 knock-in, four arms of 15 animals, with T-cell receptor sequencing of tumor and draining nodes at day 14. All spatial data and segmentation masks will be deposited publicly.

title: Closing gaps in comprehensive genomic profiling and receipt of matched therapy in advanced non-small cell lung cancer

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Matched targeted therapy improves survival in advanced lung adenocarcinoma only if the alteration is found and the drug is started. Both steps fail often. In community settings, 30 to 40 percent of patients with newly diagnosed non-squamous disease never undergo broad molecular profiling, and among those with an actionable result, 15 to 25 percent never receive the matched agent. Failures cluster by race, insurance status, rurality, and practice volume, and the reasons differ by step: tissue adequacy and ordering practice govern testing, while turnaround time, prior authorization, and treatment already started govern receipt. This project will measure both steps across a 12,000-patient multi-payer cohort, identify the modifiable determinants specific to each, and test a practice-level intervention combining reflex ordering at pathology sign-out with blood-based profiling drawn at the first oncology visit.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Measure the two-step cascade. Across 12,000 patients diagnosed between 2018 and 2023 in a linked electronic health record and claims resource, we will estimate the proportion completing profiling within 8 weeks of diagnosis and the proportion with an actionable result who start matched therapy within 12 weeks, stratified by race, ethnicity, insurance, rurality, and practice volume. Aim 2. Identify step-specific determinants using mediation analysis, testing whether tissue adequacy explains the profiling gap and whether turnaround time and early initiation of chemotherapy explain the receipt gap. Aim 3. Test an intervention in a stepped-wedge design across 18 community practices, in which pathology sign-out triggers automatic panel ordering and a blood sample is drawn at the first oncology visit, with the primary endpoint being matched therapy started within 12 weeks.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: The therapeutic advances of the last decade in this disease are real but conditional. A patient with an exon 19 deletion who never has a panel ordered receives carboplatin and pemetrexed and does no better than a patient in 2005. The magnitude of the loss is large: with roughly 40 percent of non-squamous lung adenocarcinoma harboring an alteration matched to an approved drug, a 20 percent failure rate in the cascade corresponds to thousands of patients annually receiving inferior therapy for reasons that have nothing to do with tumor biology. Because the two steps have distinct causes, interventions that address only one predictably underperform, which is the likely explanation for the modest effect of prior education-only programs. Quantifying and targeting each step separately is the contribution here.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: Most prior work reports a single completion rate and stops. Decomposing the cascade into ordering and receipt, and showing that the determinants differ, is a conceptual advance that directly implies a two-component intervention. Our intervention pairs a pathology-side default with a blood-side hedge, so that inadequate tissue, the most common single reason for failure, no longer terminates the pathway. The stepped-wedge design gives every participating practice the intervention while preserving internal controls, which is both ethically preferable and better powered than a parallel-arm design at this number of clusters. We also pre-specify subgroup estimates by race and rurality rather than reporting them post hoc, so that differential benefit can be detected rather than assumed.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: The cohort draws on a de-identified linked resource covering 280 practices, with abstraction of pathology and molecular reports for a 1,500-patient validation subsample to confirm algorithmic ascertainment. Time-to-event outcomes will be analyzed with competing-risk methods, treating death before profiling as a competing event. Mediation analysis will use inverse-odds weighting with bootstrapped confidence intervals. The stepped-wedge trial randomizes 18 practices to six sequences over 30 months, with an anticipated 1,400 patients; assuming baseline matched-therapy receipt of 62 percent and an intracluster correlation of 0.03, the design has 84 percent power to detect an absolute increase of 10 percentage points. Implementation fidelity will be tracked monthly, and cost per additional patient treated with matched therapy will be estimated from a payer perspective.

title: Targeted degradation of oncogenic kinases as a mutation-agnostic strategy in lung cancer

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Every inhibitor developed for EGFR and ALK ultimately fails because the pocket it occupies can be remodeled. Sequential generations of chemistry have answered T790M with osimertinib and G1202R with lorlatinib, only to be answered in turn by C797S and by compound alleles. Heterobifunctional molecules that recruit an E3 ligase and eliminate the target protein escape this cycle in principle, because catalytic removal of the protein does not require sustained occupancy of a functional site and can tolerate substantial remodeling of the binding surface. Preliminary compounds built from a cereblon ligand and a reversible EGFR binder reduce receptor protein by more than 90 percent within four hours in cells carrying L858R with T790M and C797S, with sustained suppression of downstream signaling. This project will optimize these molecules, define the determinants of ligase selectivity in lung epithelium, and establish whether escape from removal differs qualitatively from escape from inhibition.

sections.name: Specific Aims
sections.text: Aim 1. Optimize heterobifunctional molecules against the full allelic spectrum. We will iterate linker composition and exit vector to maximize ternary complex cooperativity, with degradation DC50 below 30 nM and maximal reduction above 90 percent across nine EGFR alleles and six ALK alleles including compound alleles. Aim 2. Define ligase dependency and its liabilities. We will compare cereblon-recruiting and VHL-recruiting series across a panel of tumor models, measure ligase expression in normal and malignant lung tissue, and determine whether loss of ligase components is a viable route to escape by conducting resistance selections in vitro. Aim 3. Determine what escape looks like. Models will be treated to regrowth, with recovered tumors profiled for ligase alterations, target amplification, and alternative receptor engagement, and compared directly with escape from inhibitor-treated controls.

sections.name: Significance
sections.text: The last fifteen years of drug development in this disease have followed a single pattern: a resistant allele appears, a more potent compound answers it, another allele appears. Each cycle takes five to seven years and delivers roughly ten months of additional benefit. A modality whose activity does not depend on the geometry of the binding pocket would break the cycle, and would be immediately relevant to the patients for whom no inhibitor exists, including those with C797S in trans and those with two substitutions in the ALK kinase domain. The Aim 2 work also addresses a general concern about this modality that has not been tested seriously in solid tumors, namely whether the requirement for an intact ligase creates a new and easily acquired escape route, as has been observed in hematologic settings.

sections.name: Innovation
sections.text: We evaluate a new modality against the specific alleles for which existing chemistry has failed, rather than against sensitive parental cells where any active compound looks good. The head-to-head comparison of escape from removal versus escape from inhibition, run in the same models under matched suppression of downstream signaling, is to our knowledge the first such experiment in an oncogene-driven solid tumor, and it tests the central claim made for this modality rather than assuming it. We also profile ligase expression across normal lung and airway epithelium to anticipate on-target toxicity in the tissue where the receptor is physiologically required, an analysis usually deferred until animals are already dosed.

sections.name: Approach
sections.text: Compound series will be synthesized in parallel with variation at three vectors and characterized by ternary complex formation using time-resolved fluorescence energy transfer, cooperativity measured as alpha, and cellular protein loss quantified by capillary immunoassay and by targeted mass spectrometry. Allelic panels will use isogenic Ba/F3 and immortalized lung epithelial lines plus twelve tumor models from donors, including four with compound ALK alleles. Resistance selections will be run at 3 and 10 times DC50 with 10^8 cells per condition, with recovered clones sequenced at CRBN, CUL4A, DDB1, RBX1, and NEDD8-pathway genes. In vivo studies use implanted tumors dosed for up to 20 weeks with 10 animals per arm, with target protein levels confirmed in tumor lysates at 4 and 24 hours after dosing to establish the relationship between suppression duration and antitumor effect.

title: Allelic phase of EGFR C797S determines activity of allosteric inhibition and of inhibitor combinations

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Acquisition of C797S is the most common on-target mechanism of progression on osimertinib, but its therapeutic implications depend on whether it resides on the same allele as T790M or on the reciprocal one, a distinction that short-read panels cannot resolve. We applied targeted long-read sequencing to 188 progression specimens and phased tertiary alleles in 41 of the 44 cases carrying C797S. The substitution was in cis with T790M in 29 cases, in trans in 8, and arose on a T790M-negative background in 4. Isogenic models recapitulating each configuration showed that the trans configuration remained sensitive to a first-generation plus third-generation inhibitor pair, with cellular IC50 of 34 nM, whereas the cis configuration was refractory to every approved agent and to all pairwise combinations tested. An allosteric compound, DFC-114, inhibited the cis triple mutant with IC50 of 18 nM and 61-fold sparing of the wild-type receptor, and produced regression in models derived from two patients with the cis configuration.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Osimertinib is now given first line to most patients with advanced lung adenocarcinoma bearing exon 19 deletions or L858R, and progression is universal. Among mechanisms that leave the tumor dependent on the same receptor, substitution of the cysteine at position 797 is the most common, reported in 7 to 15 percent of progressions. Because osimertinib forms a covalent bond with that cysteine, its loss abolishes the drug entirely. Whether anything else works depends on configuration. If the tertiary substitution lies on a different allele from the gatekeeper, one allele is inhibitable by a first-generation agent and the other by a third-generation agent, so the pair suffices. If both lie on the same allele, no combination of pocket-directed agents can engage it. The precedent from ALK-rearranged disease, where two substitutions acquired on a single allele after sequential inhibitor therapy proved refractory to all six approved agents, motivated us to treat phase as the primary variable rather than as an afterthought.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Progression specimens were collected under an institutional protocol from patients with radiographic progression on osimertinib given first or second line. Genomic DNA was subjected to adaptive-sampling nanopore sequencing enriched across a 60 kilobase window spanning EGFR, achieving median on-target depth of 740-fold; phasing required at least 20 reads spanning both codons. Isogenic Ba/F3 lines expressing each of eight allelic configurations were generated by site-directed mutagenesis and verified by long-read sequencing of the integrated cassette. Viability was measured after 72 hours across nine concentrations in triplicate, and IC50 estimated by four-parameter logistic fitting. Receptor phosphorylation at Tyr1068 was quantified by capillary immunoassay. Two tumor models were established from pleural fluid and treated at 25 mg/kg twice daily for 28 days, with eight animals per arm and tumor volume as the primary endpoint.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Of 188 specimens, 44 carried C797S at a median variant allele fraction of 11 percent. Phasing succeeded in 41. The cis configuration predominated after second-line osimertinib, comprising 26 of 31 phased cases, whereas among patients treated first line the substitution arose without the gatekeeper allele in 4 of 10. Patients with the trans configuration who subsequently received a first- plus third-generation pair had an objective response rate of 4 of 7, while none of 11 patients with the cis configuration responded to any pocket-directed regimen. In isogenic systems the cis triple mutant showed IC50 above 3 micromolar for every approved agent. DFC-114 inhibited it at 18 nM with 61-fold selectivity over the wild-type receptor and suppressed Tyr1068 phosphorylation by 88 percent at 100 nM. In implanted models from two donors with the cis configuration, DFC-114 produced mean regression of 46 percent at day 28 compared with 22 percent growth under osimertinib.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: These data argue that progression reporting should include allelic phase whenever a tertiary substitution is found, since the same variant call implies either a treatable or an untreatable tumor depending on a configuration that current assays discard. A paired-biopsy analysis of the second-line registration population had previously reported that the tertiary cysteine substitution accounted for roughly one in seven progressions and that a substantial minority of specimens contained no identifiable driver of escape at all; our data extend that by showing that the treatable subset is smaller still, because most tertiary substitutions in previously treated patients occupy the same allele as the gatekeeper. The plasma survey of first-line failure similarly found that tertiary substitutions arise more often on a gatekeeper-negative background, which our phasing confirms and which predicts sensitivity to agents that do not require the cysteine. Limitations include the modest number of trans cases and the absence of prospective treatment assignment by configuration.

title: Plasma genomic landscape of progression on first-line osimertinib in advanced lung adenocarcinoma

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: The spectrum of escape from osimertinib given first line differs from that seen after prior exposure to earlier-generation agents, but has been described only in small series. We analyzed circulating tumor DNA at baseline and at radiographic progression in 271 patients receiving first-line osimertinib, using a 129-gene panel with unique molecular identifiers. Baseline tumor DNA was detectable in 84 percent. At progression, MET copy gain was the most common finding, in 41 patients or 15 percent, followed by tertiary EGFR substitution at codon 797 in 19 patients or 7 percent, ERBB2 amplification in 5 percent, and oncogenic fusions involving RET, ALK, or BRAF in 4 percent. The gatekeeper allele was absent in all but three cases. No identifiable alteration was found in 122 patients, or 45 percent. Two or more independent alterations coexisted in 38 patients, and their subsequent progression-free survival on next therapy was shorter, at 3.1 versus 5.9 months.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: When osimertinib is given after a first-generation agent, the tumor entering therapy has already been shaped by selection for the gatekeeper allele, and progression frequently involves loss or retention of that allele alongside a tertiary substitution. Given first line, the drug meets an unselected tumor, and there is no reason to expect the same spectrum. Earlier work in the second-line setting found the gatekeeper allele retained in a majority of progression specimens and tied a substantial fraction of escape to that lineage; the first-line setting has no such history. Understanding the difference matters practically, because it determines what a clinician should test for at progression and which salvage trials are worth opening. Blood-based profiling is the only feasible way to assemble a cohort of this size, since fewer than half of patients undergo repeat biopsy, but it under-detects copy gain and cannot see morphologic change, and those limitations must be kept in view when interpreting the 45 percent of patients in whom nothing was found.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Patients starting first-line osimertinib at 14 centers were enrolled prospectively between 2017 and 2019. Blood was collected at baseline, at 6 weeks, and within 4 weeks of investigator-assessed progression, into cell-stabilizing tubes and processed within 6 hours. Sequencing used a 129-gene hybrid capture panel to median unique depth of 14,800-fold, with a limit of detection of 0.1 percent variant allele fraction for substitutions and copy gain called at ratio above 2.1 with at least 40 percent tumor fraction. Alterations were classified as on-target, bypass, downstream, or fusion. Progression-free survival on subsequent therapy was measured from the start of the next regimen. Association between alteration count and subsequent survival used Cox regression adjusted for age, performance status, and baseline tumor fraction.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Median follow-up was 26 months and 271 patients had evaluable paired samples. Median progression-free survival on osimertinib was 18.4 months. At progression, on-target substitutions occurred in 24 patients, of whom 19 had C797S and 5 had L718Q or G724S. Copy gain at the MET locus was seen in 41, with a median ratio of 3.4. ERBB2 amplification occurred in 14, activating PIK3CA mutations in 12, KRAS mutations in 8, and fusions in 11. Cell cycle gene alterations, chiefly CCNE1 amplification and CDKN2A loss, were present in 21. In 122 patients no alteration meeting our criteria was detected; these patients had lower baseline tumor fraction, at a median of 1.2 versus 4.7 percent, suggesting under-detection contributes. Patients with two or more coexisting alterations, 38 in total, had shorter subsequent progression-free survival, with hazard ratio 1.74 and 95 percent confidence interval 1.15 to 2.63.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Three findings have immediate implications. First, the gatekeeper allele is essentially absent when osimertinib is used first line, so assays and trials designed around it are misdirected in this population. Second, copy gain at the MET locus is the single most common actionable event, which supports the ongoing evaluation of paired receptor blockade in this setting. Third, nearly half of patients have no detectable alteration in blood, and these patients are enriched for low tumor shedding; tissue sampling in that subgroup is likely to reveal morphologic change that blood cannot show, as suggested by the concurrent observation that antecedent RB1 and TP53 inactivation identifies tumors prone to a phenotypic switch. The finding that multiple coexisting alterations predict shorter benefit from the next line supports counting events rather than reporting only the dominant one. Limitations include reliance on a single blood draw at progression and the absence of matched tissue in most patients.

title: Savolitinib plus osimertinib after progression with high-level MET copy gain: efficacy and determinants of response

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Focal amplification of the MET receptor reactivates ERK and AKT output despite continued EGFR blockade and is the most common actionable event at progression on osimertinib. We report a multicenter phase 2 study, NCT03778229, in which 118 patients with progression and centrally confirmed high-level copy gain received savolitinib 300 mg daily with osimertinib 80 mg daily. The confirmed objective response rate was 49 percent, with median duration of response 9.1 months and median progression-free survival 8.2 months. Response was strongly related to the degree of copy gain: 62 percent among patients with a signal intensity ratio of 5 or higher versus 28 percent below that threshold. Co-occurring TP53 mutation was associated with shorter benefit. Among 34 patients with paired specimens at second progression, secondary kinase-domain substitutions in MET, chiefly D1228N and Y1230C, were found in 12, further copy gain in 6, and events unrelated to either receptor in 11.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: The logic of paired receptor blockade is straightforward: when a second receptor restores signaling that the primary inhibitor has shut down, inhibiting both should restore control. The practical difficulty has been defining which tumors are genuinely dependent on the second receptor. Copy gain is continuous, and trials have used thresholds ranging from a gene copy number of 5 to 10 or a signal intensity ratio above 2, producing reported response rates from 30 to 66 percent that are difficult to compare. Concordance work comparing in situ hybridization with sequencing-based copy calling showed that a nominal gene copy number of 5 corresponds to widely varying ratios and to inconsistent receptor protein expression, which is why we required both a ratio of at least 2 and a copy number of at least 10 for entry, and why we pre-specified an analysis of response across the range of copy gain within that enriched population.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Eligible patients had EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma progressing on osimertinib with central confirmation of copy gain on a progression biopsy by dual-color in situ hybridization. Treatment continued until progression or unacceptable toxicity. The primary endpoint was confirmed objective response by RECIST 1.1 with independent central review; 118 patients provided 90 percent power to exclude a null response rate of 25 percent against an alternative of 40 percent. Blood was collected at baseline, every 6 weeks, and at progression for 129-gene sequencing. Second progression biopsies were requested from all patients. Exploratory analyses related response to ratio, to co-occurring alterations, and to receptor protein expression measured by quantitative immunofluorescence in the entry specimen.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Between 2019 and 2021, 118 patients were treated; median age was 63 and 61 percent were female. Sixty patients had a ratio of 5 or greater. Confirmed responses occurred in 58 patients overall, 49 percent, with 37 of 60 in the high-ratio group and 21 of 58 below it, a difference of 34 percentage points. Median progression-free survival was 8.2 months overall, 10.4 months in the high-ratio group and 5.6 months below it, with hazard ratio 0.52. Among 41 patients with TP53 mutation, median progression-free survival was 6.1 versus 11.0 months in wild-type, hazard ratio 1.86. Grade 3 or higher events occurred in 41 percent, most commonly neutropenia, transaminase elevation, and peripheral edema; 12 percent discontinued for toxicity. At second progression, secondary substitutions in the MET kinase domain were the most common single finding, in 12 of 34 evaluable patients.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Paired blockade converts a poorly responsive population into one with a response rate approaching that of front-line targeted therapy, but only when the second receptor is genuinely load-bearing, and degree of copy gain remains the best available proxy for that. Our data support a two-part entry criterion rather than either measure alone. The pattern at second progression is instructive: substitutions within the kinase domain of the second receptor dominate, exactly as occurred historically with the primary receptor, which suggests that the same escalation of chemistry will be required and that agents active against D1228 and Y1230 substitutions should be prioritized. That roughly a third of second progressions involved neither receptor is a reminder that dual blockade selects for lineages that have abandoned receptor dependence entirely. Limitations include the single-arm design and the requirement for tissue, which excluded patients too frail for biopsy.

title: Concordance of MET copy number assessment by in situ hybridization, hybrid capture sequencing, and immunohistochemistry in progression biopsies

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Thresholds for MET copy gain differ across assays and trials, and the resulting cohorts are not comparable. We assessed 214 progression biopsies from patients with EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma using dual-color in situ hybridization, a 523-gene hybrid capture panel, and immunohistochemistry with two antibody clones, all performed on serial sections from the same block. Agreement between hybridization ratio above 2 and sequencing-based copy number above 5 was moderate, with Cohen kappa 0.61. Discordance was concentrated in specimens with tumor purity below 30 percent, where sequencing systematically under-called gain, and in specimens with chromosome 7 polysomy, where hybridization over-called it. Protein expression correlated with copy number only above a copy number of 10, with Spearman rho 0.71 above that value and 0.19 below it. We provide a calibration table permitting retrospective harmonization of published cohorts and recommend reporting both ratio and absolute copy number.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Assay choice is not a neutral technical detail when the analyte is a continuous variable and the clinical decision is binary. Copy gain at the MET locus illustrates this vividly: the same tumor can be called amplified by one method and not by another, and published response rates in trials of paired receptor blockade correlate as strongly with entry assay as with any biological variable. Prior work established that copy gain is a recurrent event at progression on EGFR-directed therapy and estimated its frequency at 15 to 20 percent, but the frequency estimate inherits whatever threshold the study used. Our purpose here is narrow and deliberately methodological: to quantify agreement among the three assays used in practice, to identify the specimen characteristics that drive disagreement, and to provide a conversion that makes existing literature interpretable. We do not address which threshold predicts benefit, which requires treated cohorts.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Consecutive progression biopsies with at least 20 percent tumor nuclei were retrieved from three institutional archives. Serial sections were cut for each assay in a fixed order to minimize block depletion effects. Hybridization used probes to the MET locus and the chromosome 7 centromere, with 60 nuclei scored per case by two observers blinded to other results; discordant cases were re-scored jointly. Sequencing used a 523-gene panel with copy number called from normalized coverage against a pooled reference, adjusted for purity estimated from allele fractions. Immunohistochemistry used clones SP44 and D1C2 scored by H-score. Agreement was summarized by Cohen kappa and by Bland-Altman analysis of log ratios. Purity and polysomy were pre-specified as candidate modifiers and tested by interaction terms in linear models.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Of 214 specimens, 198 yielded results from all three assays. Forty-one were called amplified by hybridization ratio and 33 by sequencing, with 27 called by both, giving kappa 0.61 and 95 percent confidence interval 0.48 to 0.74. Among 46 specimens with purity below 30 percent, sequencing called gain in 4 while hybridization called it in 11. Chromosome 7 polysomy, defined as centromere signal above 3 with ratio below 2, was present in 29 specimens and accounted for 8 of 14 hybridization-positive, sequencing-negative discordances. H-score correlated with copy number weakly overall, rho 0.44, but the relationship was driven entirely by the high end: rho 0.71 for copy number above 10 and 0.19 below. Both antibody clones agreed with each other, rho 0.86. Inter-observer agreement for hybridization scoring was 0.79.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: The practical message is that ratio and absolute copy number carry different information and that reporting one alone discards the other. Sequencing under-calls in low-purity specimens because normalized coverage is diluted, which matters because progression biopsies are frequently small core or fine-needle samples. Hybridization over-calls when the whole chromosome is gained, which is biologically distinct from focal amplification and, in the few treated patients in our archive, was not associated with response. Protein expression is not a substitute for either method below high-level gain. Our calibration table allows an investigator reading a trial that enrolled at copy number 5 to estimate what fraction of that cohort would have met a ratio-based criterion. Limitations include the retrospective design, absence of systematic treatment data, and the fact that fixation conditions varied across archives.

title: Lipid peroxide detoxification sustains the surviving tumor reservoir during continuous EGFR inhibition

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Deep responses to EGFR inhibition leave a small population of viable cells that neither proliferate nor die while drug is present, and from which regrowth eventually arises. We characterized this reservoir across six EGFR-driven lung adenocarcinoma models exposed continuously to gefitinib or osimertinib for 14 days. Surviving cells retained the founding driver allele, acquired no new kinase-domain variants, and returned to full drug sensitivity within three weeks of drug withdrawal, establishing that their survival is not heritably encoded. They exhibited a coordinated shift toward polyunsaturated fatty acid incorporation, elevated C11-BODIPY oxidation, and strict dependence on GPX4: pharmacologic or genetic GPX4 inactivation eliminated 92 percent of surviving cells within 72 hours, an effect fully rescued by ferrostatin-1. In implanted tumors, adding a GPX4 inhibitor at maximal response extended time to regrowth from 41 to 96 days without deepening the initial regression.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: The characteristic shape of the response curve to oncogene-directed therapy is a steep decline followed by a long plateau. The plateau is not the absence of tumor; it is a residual population held in check. Two questions follow. What allows those cells to survive an inhibitor that kills their neighbors, and can they be eliminated while they are few. Prior work has emphasized chromatin changes, notably a KDM5A-associated repressed state, and has shown that surviving cells are reversibly rather than heritably altered. Metabolic vulnerability has been less explored in this setting, although the combination of a slow-cycling state and a shifted membrane lipid composition is precisely the configuration that renders cells dependent on peroxide detoxification. We therefore asked whether the surviving reservoir in EGFR-driven models is dependent on GPX4, and whether exploiting that dependence at the point of maximal response lengthens the plateau.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Six models were used, three established lines and three grown from patient tumors, carrying exon 19 deletion or L858R with or without the gatekeeper allele. Cells were exposed to 1 micromolar gefitinib or 300 nM osimertinib continuously for 14 days with medium changed every 48 hours. Surviving cells were enumerated by nuclear counting and characterized by RNA sequencing, lipidomics by mass spectrometry, and C11-BODIPY flow cytometry. GPX4 was inactivated with RSL3 at 500 nM or by two independent guide RNAs. Rescue used ferrostatin-1 at 2 micromolar. Reversibility was tested by withdrawing drug and re-measuring IC50 at 7, 14, and 21 days. In vivo, tumors from three donors were implanted in NSG mice, treated with osimertinib for 28 days to maximal regression, then randomized to continued osimertinib with or without RSL3 analog, 12 animals per arm, followed to a regrowth threshold of twice nadir volume.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Continuous exposure reduced viable cells by 96 to 99.4 percent across models, with a stable residual fraction between 0.6 and 4 percent from day 7 onward. Deep sequencing of the receptor kinase domain in surviving cells detected no variant above 0.5 percent. Withdrawal restored the parental IC50 within 21 days in all six models.
