Transcriptomes of surviving cells converged on a shared program, with 214 genes up-regulated in at least five of six models, enriched for lysosomal, autophagic, and glutathione metabolism terms. Lipidomics showed a 2.4-fold increase in polyunsaturated phosphatidylethanolamine species, and C11-BODIPY oxidation increased 3.1-fold. RSL3 eliminated 92 percent of surviving cells at 72 hours versus 11 percent of untreated parental cells, and ferrostatin-1 restored survival completely. In vivo, median time to regrowth was 96 days with the added agent versus 41 days with osimertinib alone.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: The surviving reservoir is metabolically, not genetically, distinguished, and its dependence on peroxide detoxification is a tractable liability that exists only while cells are in that state. The timing of intervention therefore matters as much as the agent: giving the second drug at progression, when the population has expanded and diversified, would be expected to fail, whereas giving it at maximal response acts on the smallest and most uniform target. A clinical series reported concurrently showed that biallelic inactivation of RB1 and TP53 precedes morphologic change by many months in patients, which suggests that the reservoir is genotypically stratified before it becomes phenotypically committed, and that the subset destined for a lineage switch may not share the vulnerability we describe. Limitations include the reliance on immunodeficient animals, which excludes any immune contribution to control of residual disease, and the short duration of the withdrawal experiments.

title: A single-cell atlas of residual disease in EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma during maximal response

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Tumors at maximal response to EGFR inhibition are rarely sampled, yet they contain the cells from which all subsequent progression arises. We profiled 214,000 individual cells from 32 specimens obtained before treatment, at maximal response between 6 and 12 weeks, and at progression, using droplet-based transcriptome capture with matched T-cell receptor sequencing. Malignant cells at maximal response occupied three recurrent transcriptional states: a diapause-like quiescent state present in all patients, an alveolar-like state expressing SFTPC and NKX2-1, and in six patients a state expressing ASCL1, INSM1, and DLL3 that was undetectable before treatment and that dominated the progression specimen in three of those six. Antigen presentation genes including B2M, TAP1, and HLA-A were coordinately suppressed at maximal response and remained suppressed at progression. Cytotoxic lymphocytes were present but confined to stromal bands and expressed high TOX and PDCD1.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Most molecular understanding of escape from targeted therapy comes from specimens taken when the tumor is already growing again. By then the population has expanded through many divisions and selection has run its course, so the earliest steps are invisible. Sampling at maximal response is technically and ethically harder, but it observes the population at its smallest. Work in cultured cells has established that the surviving population is reversibly reprogrammed rather than mutated, and has identified metabolic dependencies specific to that state. Whether the same states exist in patients, whether they are shared across individuals, and how they relate to the eventual mechanism of progression are open questions that require human material and single-cell resolution. We assembled a cohort with mandated research biopsies at three timepoints to address them.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Thirty-two patients with EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma consented to research biopsies before therapy, at radiographic maximal response, and at progression; 21 provided all three. Specimens were dissociated within 45 minutes and processed for droplet-based 3-prime transcriptome capture, targeting 8,000 cells per specimen, with paired V(D)J libraries. Malignant cells were identified by inferred copy number profiles and by expression of the driver allele where coverage permitted. States were defined by consensus non-negative matrix factorization across patients, with programs retained if recurrent in at least four patients. Antigen presentation scoring used a 22-gene module. Spatial validation used multiplexed immunofluorescence for SFTPC, ASCL1, CD8, and pan-cytokeratin on adjacent sections from all 32 specimens.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Malignant cell yield fell from a median of 3,400 cells before treatment to 410 at maximal response. Three recurrent programs were identified. The quiescent program, marked by low MKI67, elevated CDKN1A, and high lysosomal gene expression, was present in 32 of 32 response specimens and comprised a median 61 percent of malignant cells. The alveolar-like program was present in 27. A neuroendocrine program expressing ASCL1, INSM1, and DLL3 was detected in 6 of 32 response specimens, at a median 3.8 percent of malignant cells, and was absent from all matched pre-treatment specimens at a detection floor of 0.4 percent. Of those six patients, three progressed with a tumor in which that program dominated, and all three had biallelic RB1 and TP53 loss at baseline. Antigen presentation module scores fell 2.2-fold from baseline to response and did not recover. CD8 T cells were 4.1-fold more abundant in stroma than within tumor nests.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Residual disease in patients is not a uniform population held in stasis but a mixture of at least three states, only one of which appears poised for a lineage switch. The dependence of surviving cells on lipid peroxide detoxification, first shown in continuously exposed cultures where a ferroptosis inhibitor fully rescued death caused by GPX4 inactivation, maps onto our quiescent program, which shares its lysosomal and glutathione signature; this suggests the cultured phenomenon is a faithful model of the dominant state but not of the minority state expressing neuroendocrine transcription factors. The coordinated suppression of antigen presentation at maximal response offers a straightforward explanation for why checkpoint blockade added at that point has not helped these patients. Limitations include the small number of patients with all three timepoints and the possibility that dissociation biases against fragile cells.

title: Biallelic RB1 and TP53 inactivation identifies EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma at risk of neuroendocrine conversion

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: A minority of EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinomas progress on inhibitor therapy with a repeat biopsy that no longer resembles the original tumor, showing small cells with molded nuclei, synaptophysin and INSM1 expression, and a proliferative index above 80 percent while retaining the founding EGFR allele. We analyzed 388 patients with baseline sequencing and at least one progression biopsy. Concurrent biallelic inactivation of RB1 and TP53 was present at baseline in 47 patients, 12 percent. Among those, 19 percent underwent conversion within 3 years, compared with 0.7 percent of patients without both events, a relative risk of 27. Median time from starting therapy to conversion was 17.8 months. Overall survival after conversion was 10.3 months despite platinum-etoposide, with an objective response rate to that regimen of 54 percent but a median duration of only 3.4 months.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Progression on EGFR-directed therapy is usually explained by a second genomic alteration, but in a subset of patients the tumor changes what it is rather than how it signals. The converted tumor retains the founding driver, proving descent from the original clone, yet no longer depends on the receptor and does not respond to any receptor-directed agent. Because recognition requires tissue, and because most progression events are worked up in blood or not at all, the true frequency is uncertain and probably understated. In the largest paired-biopsy series reported to date, a substantial minority of progression specimens showed no identifiable genomic mechanism, a fraction that plausibly includes tumors whose escape is phenotypic. If a baseline genotype identified patients at risk, re-biopsy could be targeted rather than universal, and prevention trials would have an enrollable population.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Patients with advanced EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma treated at two institutions between 2010 and 2018 with baseline tumor sequencing on a 468-gene panel and at least one post-progression biopsy were included. Biallelic inactivation was defined as a truncating or deleterious missense variant with loss of the remaining allele inferred from allele-specific copy number, or homozygous deletion. Conversion was defined by central pathology review requiring compatible morphology plus positivity for at least two of synaptophysin, chromogranin, and INSM1, with retention of the founding EGFR allele confirmed by sequencing of the converted specimen. Cumulative incidence of conversion was estimated with death and non-converting progression as competing events, and compared by Gray test. Survival after conversion was measured from the date of the diagnostic biopsy.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Of 388 patients, 47 had biallelic inactivation of both genes at baseline, 96 had one, and 245 had neither. Conversion occurred in 9 patients with both events, 1 with one event, and 2 with neither; the 3-year cumulative incidence was 19.4 percent versus 0.7 percent, Gray test p less than 0.001. All converted specimens retained the founding allele, and 11 of 12 retained it at a variant allele fraction above 30 percent. Time from initiation of therapy to conversion ranged from 5.6 to 41 months, median 17.8. Nine patients received platinum-etoposide, with responses in 5 and a median duration of 3.4 months. Median overall survival from conversion was 10.3 months, 95 percent confidence interval 6.9 to 15.1. Serum chromogranin A rose above the upper limit of normal in 7 of 9 patients tested, with a median lead time of 6 weeks before the diagnostic biopsy.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: A simple baseline genotype available from routine sequencing identifies a group in which the risk of a phenotypic switch is roughly 27-fold higher than baseline, which is sufficient to justify a targeted re-biopsy policy and provides an enrollable population for prevention studies. The long interval between loss of the two tumor suppressors and the appearance of the new phenotype argues that these lesions are permissive rather than sufficient, and that a second, probably epigenetic, step intervenes. Work in cultured cells describing a reversibly reprogrammed reservoir that survives continuous inhibition offers a plausible location for that step, since a persistent non-dividing population would have time to reorganize its chromatin under selection. Practically, our data argue against universal re-biopsy and in favor of a genotype-directed policy, and support monitoring chromogranin A in the at-risk group. Limitations include retrospective ascertainment and biopsy at the discretion of treating physicians.

title: An ASCL1-dependent enhancer program licenses conversion of Egfr-driven lung tumors to a neuroendocrine state

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Conversion of lung adenocarcinoma to a small cell phenotype during EGFR inhibition is well documented in patients but has lacked a tractable model. We generated mice bearing inducible EgfrL858R with conditional Rb1 and Trp53 alleles and lineage tracing from Sftpc. Under continuous osimertinib, 43 percent of animals developed tumors that were synaptophysin- and INSM1-positive, expressed ASCL1, and retained the lineage label, proving descent from alveolar type 2 cells rather than expansion of a pre-existing neuroendocrine population. Single-nucleus multiome profiling showed that conversion is preceded by loss of H3K27 trimethylation across a 340-enhancer ASCL1-associated domain, detectable four weeks before any morphologic change. EZH2 inhibition accelerated conversion, from 43 to 71 percent, whereas LSD1 inhibition reduced it to 9 percent and prevented enhancer de-repression. Established converted tumors were unaffected by either agent, indicating that the state becomes fixed.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Escape routes that depend on kinase-domain chemistry can be answered with better chemistry. A tumor that abandons receptor dependence altogether cannot. Human series have established the clinical contours of this phenomenon: it occurs in a few percent of patients, the founding driver is retained, the outcome is poor, and it is preceded by inactivation of two tumor suppressors. The clinical observation that RB1 and TP53 are lost long before any morphologic change, with a median interval approaching a year and a half between the start of therapy and the diagnostic biopsy, implies an intervening step that is not written in the genome. Testing that hypothesis requires an animal in which the permissive genotype is fixed but the switch itself remains stochastic and can therefore be measured as a frequency and modified pharmacologically.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Mice carrying tetO-EgfrL858R, CCSP-rtTA, Rb1 fl/fl, Trp53 fl/fl, and Sftpc-CreER with a tdTomato reporter were induced with doxycycline and tamoxifen at 8 weeks. Tumors were confirmed by micro-computed tomography at 12 weeks, after which animals received osimertinib 25 mg/kg daily for up to 40 weeks. Cohorts of 22 to 26 animals received vehicle, tazemetostat 250 mg/kg twice daily, or an LSD1 inhibitor at 5 mg/kg daily in addition. Tumors were scored blinded for morphology, synaptophysin, INSM1, and reporter retention. Single-nucleus multiome libraries were prepared from 6 animals per timepoint at 0, 4, 12, and 24 weeks of therapy, targeting 5,000 nuclei each. Enhancer domains were defined by consensus ATAC peaks with differential H3K27me3 measured by CUT and RUN.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Of 26 vehicle-treated animals followed to 40 weeks, 11 developed neuroendocrine tumors, all reporter-positive and all retaining the induced allele by genotyping. Conversion was never observed in animals with intact Rb1. Multiome profiling of pre-conversion tumors at 12 weeks identified a subset of nuclei, median 2.6 percent, with open chromatin at ASCL1-proximal enhancers but no detectable ASCL1 transcript, a configuration absent at week 0. H3K27me3 across the 340-enhancer domain fell 3.4-fold between weeks 4 and 12. Tazemetostat raised conversion frequency to 71 percent, 17 of 24 animals, and accelerated median time to conversion from 31 to 19 weeks. The LSD1 inhibitor lowered it to 9 percent, 2 of 22, with preserved H3K27me3 and no open chromatin at the domain. In animals with established converted tumors, neither agent altered growth.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Conversion proceeds through a licensing step defined by de-repression of a specific enhancer domain, occurring weeks before any change visible to a pathologist, and it is pharmacologically modifiable only during that window. That EZH2 inhibition accelerates the switch is a cautionary result, since such agents have been proposed as combination partners in this disease on unrelated grounds. Our single-cell data also connect to the human observation of a minority population expressing neuroendocrine transcription factors within residual disease at maximal response, detectable in roughly a fifth of patients sampled at that point and absent before treatment; the mouse shows that such cells arise from alveolar progenitors under drug pressure rather than pre-existing. Limitations include the artificial nature of doxycycline- driven expression and the fact that our animals lack the co-mutational complexity of human tumors.

title: Amivantamab in EGFR exon 20 insertion non-small cell lung cancer after platinum-based chemotherapy

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Insertions in the region following the C-helix of EGFR confer minimal sensitivity to approved kinase inhibitors. Amivantamab is an immunoglobulin engaging the EGFR ectodomain and MET simultaneously, acting through receptor internalization and antibody-dependent effector function rather than through the ATP pocket. In this multicenter study, NCT04988295, 124 patients with insertion-bearing lung adenocarcinoma who had progressed after platinum chemotherapy received amivantamab 1050 mg weekly then biweekly. The confirmed objective response rate by independent review was 40 percent, with median duration of response 11.1 months, median progression-free survival 8.3 months, and median overall survival 22.8 months. Responses occurred across insertion positions, including 6 of 17 patients with insertions after residue 773. Infusion-related reactions occurred in 66 percent, almost entirely with the first infusion, and rash in 86 percent, grade 3 in 4 percent.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Patients with insertions in this region are told they have EGFR-mutant lung cancer and are frequently given an inhibitor that works for two years in patients with exon 19 deletions and for three months in them. The reason is structural: these alleles adopt an active conformation without enlarging the drug cleft, so agents optimized against the classical alleles lose one to two orders of magnitude of potency while retaining full activity against the wild-type receptor, and dose escalation is limited by rash and diarrhea before tumor concentrations are reached. Comprehensive surveys of escape from third-generation therapy have documented how thoroughly the field has optimized around the classical alleles, and by implication how little of that effort transfers here. An agent that removes the receptor from the surface, rather than competing for a cleft that is too small, sidesteps the constraint entirely.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Eligible patients had locally advanced or metastatic lung adenocarcinoma with an insertion in EGFR identified locally, progression after platinum-based chemotherapy, and measurable disease. Amivantamab was given intravenously at 1050 mg for patients under 80 kg and 1400 mg at or above, weekly for four weeks then every two weeks, with split first dosing over two days and mandatory premedication. The primary endpoint was confirmed objective response by blinded independent central review using RECIST 1.1. Secondary endpoints included duration of response, progression-free and overall survival, and safety. Baseline plasma was sequenced centrally to confirm insertion identity and to characterize co-occurring alterations. With 124 patients, the lower bound of the 95 percent confidence interval excluded a response rate of 25 percent.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Between 2018 and 2020, 124 patients were treated; median age 62, 61 percent female, 49 percent Asian, median two prior lines. Insertions occurred in the near loop in 89 patients and the far loop in 35. Confirmed responses were seen in 50 patients, 40 percent, with 3 complete responses. Median duration of response was 11.1 months and 47 percent of responders remained in response at 12 months. Median progression-free survival was 8.3 months and median overall survival 22.8 months. Response rate was 41 percent in near-loop and 35 percent in far-loop insertions. Among 41 patients with baseline intracranial disease, the intracranial response rate was 22 percent. Infusion-related reactions occurred in 82 patients, 66 percent, with 3 percent grade 3 or higher; rash occurred in 107 patients and paronychia in 45. Treatment was discontinued for adverse events in 10 percent.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: An agent that depletes the receptor rather than occupying its cleft produces durable benefit in a population for which pocket-directed chemistry has consistently failed, and the activity is largely independent of insertion position, which is what one would predict for a mechanism that does not depend on pocket geometry. The response rate of 40 percent nonetheless leaves the majority without benefit, and the median duration near a year indicates that escape occurs. Whether that reflects incomplete receptor removal, limited effector cell availability, or engagement of other receptors is unresolved and is being addressed in correlative work. Intracranial activity was modest, consistent with the limited access of a large immunoglobulin to that compartment, and argues for pairing with an agent that reaches it. Infusion reactions are frequent but manageable and confined to the first dose. Limitations include the single-arm design and local rather than central insertion identification at enrollment.

title: Structure-guided design of an exon 20 insertion-selective EGFR inhibitor with wild-type sparing and brain exposure

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Approved EGFR inhibitors fail against C-helix loop insertions because these alleles are constitutively active without enlarging the drug cleft, so selectivity over the wild-type receptor collapses and tolerable doses do not engage the target. We solved crystal structures of four insertion-bearing kinase domains at 2.1 to 2.6 angstrom and found that the inserted residues shift the C-helix inward and reduce pocket volume by 18 to 27 cubic angstrom relative to wild type, with the deficit concentrated near the back pocket. Guided by these differences we developed SRX-2109, which occupies the contracted pocket and makes a hydrogen bond to the inserted asparagine present in the most common alleles. SRX-2109 inhibits insertion-bearing receptors at cellular IC50 of 12 to 41 nM with 38-fold sparing of wild type, achieves an unbound brain to plasma ratio of 0.51, and produces regression in five of six tumor models including two intracranial implants.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: The therapeutic problem in this genotype is a ratio, not a potency. Compounds that inhibit insertion-bearing receptors in biochemical assays already exist; what does not exist is a compound that does so at concentrations achievable without inhibiting the receptor in skin and gut. Antibody-based approaches sidestep the pocket entirely, and the registrational experience with a dual-targeting immunoglobulin in this population established a benchmark response rate of 40 percent with a median duration of 11 months and only modest intracranial activity. A small molecule with genuine selectivity would complement that, particularly for intracranial disease, where a large protein has limited access. We therefore treated the wild-type sparing ratio as the primary design objective and used structural differences among individual insertions rather than treating them as a single class.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Kinase domain constructs bearing V769_D770insASV, D770_N771insSVD, H773_V774insNPH, and N771_P772insH were expressed in insect cells, purified, and crystallized with and without ligand. Diffraction data were collected at 100 K and structures refined to R-free below 0.24. Pocket volumes were computed with a rolling probe of 1.4 angstrom radius. Selectivity was measured in isogenic Ba/F3 pairs and confirmed in immortalized bronchial epithelial cells and in primary keratinocytes as a skin surrogate. Unbound brain partitioning was determined by equilibrium dialysis of brain homogenate and plasma with steady-state dosing. Efficacy used six models grown from patient tumors, four subcutaneous and two implanted intracranially with bioluminescent tracking, 10 animals per arm, dosed at 15 mg/kg daily for 28 days.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: All four insertions produced an inward shift of the C-helix of 1.4 to 2.2 angstrom, with pocket volume reduced by 18 to 27 cubic angstrom. Osimertinib retained wild-type potency of 8 nM while losing potency against insertions, 310 to 1,180 nM, giving selectivity ratios below 0.05. SRX-2109 inhibited the four alleles at 12, 19, 27, and 41 nM with wild-type IC50 of 780 nM, a selectivity ratio of 38 against the most sensitive allele. Keratinocyte receptor phosphorylation was unaffected at 300 nM. Unbound brain to plasma ratio was 0.51 at steady state, compared with 0.06 for a clinical comparator. In subcutaneous models, mean tumor regression at day 28 was 58 percent versus 12 percent growth under osimertinib; in intracranial models, median survival was 61 versus 34 days. Regrowth tumors from two models acquired T790M-analogous gatekeeper substitutions.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Treating selectivity as the design objective rather than as a downstream property yields a compound that can plausibly be dosed to a concentration that matters in patients. The structural basis is specific: a contracted back pocket accommodates a smaller substituent, and the inserted asparagine present in the two most common alleles provides a hydrogen bond that the wild-type receptor cannot make, converting the insertion from a liability into a recognition element. Brain exposure adds a capability that receptor-depleting antibodies lack, and the two approaches are therefore complementary rather than competing. The emergence of gatekeeper-analogous substitutions in regrowth tumors is expected and indicates that this compound will follow the same trajectory as earlier generations unless paired. Limitations include the absence of clinical data and the fact that two less common insertions were not structurally characterized.

title: Lorlatinib versus crizotinib in previously untreated advanced ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Lorlatinib is a third-generation ALK inhibitor with activity against most single kinase-domain substitutions and substantial central nervous system exposure. In this open-label study, 296 patients with previously untreated advanced ALK-positive lung adenocarcinoma were assigned 1:1 to lorlatinib 100 mg daily or crizotinib 250 mg twice daily. At the primary analysis, progression-free survival by blinded independent review favored lorlatinib, with hazard ratio 0.28 and 95 percent confidence interval 0.19 to 0.41; median was not reached versus 9.3 months. Objective response occurred in 76 percent versus 58 percent. Among 30 and 32 patients with measurable intracranial lesions, intracranial response occurred in 82 percent versus 23 percent, and the cumulative incidence of progression in that compartment at 12 months was 2.8 percent versus 33 percent. Hypercholesterolemia occurred in 70 percent and cognitive effects in 21 percent, generally reversible with dose modification.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Fusion-driven lung adenocarcinoma is exquisitely sensitive to kinase inhibition, and the sequential introduction of successively more potent agents has extended median survival beyond five years. Two problems have persisted. Disease in the neuraxis has historically been the dominant site of failure, because early agents are efflux substrates and achieve negligible concentrations beyond the endothelium. And each additional line of therapy raises the probability that the tumor accumulates two substitutions within the same kinase domain, a configuration catalogued in post-progression series and refractory to every approved agent. Using the most potent and best-penetrating agent first is one way to address both, but it has been argued that doing so merely selects for the worst alleles earlier. This trial tests the efficacy half of that question.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Patients with stage IIIB or IV disease and a locally confirmed ALK rearrangement, no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease, and ECOG performance status 0 to 2 were assigned 1:1 with stratification by ethnicity and presence of intracranial disease. Imaging including dedicated brain magnetic resonance imaging was performed every 8 weeks. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival by blinded independent central review; 296 patients provided 85 percent power to detect a hazard ratio of 0.55 with 177 events. Intracranial endpoints were assessed by a neuroradiologist blinded to assignment. Plasma was collected at baseline and progression for 74-gene sequencing. Cognitive and mood effects were captured by protocol-specified adverse event grouping and by patient-reported instruments.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Between 2017 and 2019, 149 patients received lorlatinib and 147 crizotinib. At a median follow-up of 18.3 months, 41 and 100 events had occurred. Median progression-free survival was not reached with lorlatinib and 9.3 months with crizotinib, hazard ratio 0.28. Twelve-month progression-free survival was 78 versus 39 percent. Objective response occurred in 113 versus 85 patients. Among patients with measurable intracranial lesions, responses occurred in 25 of 30 versus 7 of 32, and complete intracranial responses in 21 versus 2. Grade 3 or 4 events occurred in 72 percent versus 56 percent, driven by lipid abnormalities; 7 percent versus 9 percent discontinued for toxicity. Cognitive effects were reported in 31 lorlatinib patients, grade 3 in 3, and resolved with dose reduction in 26. No new safety signals emerged with longer follow-up.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Using the most potent agent first produces a large improvement in disease control and a near-elimination of failure in the neuraxis during the first year. Measured unbound partitioning ratios above 0.5 for this compound, in contrast to values near 0.03 for crizotinib, provide the pharmacologic explanation and predict that the difference should persist. The unresolved question is what happens at progression: the concern that first-line use of the most potent agent selects for compound alleles that no existing drug can address is not answered by this analysis and requires the post-progression genotyping that is ongoing. Toxicity differs in kind rather than degree from earlier agents, with metabolic and neurocognitive effects predominating; these were manageable but require counseling before treatment. Overall survival data are immature.

title: Compound ALK kinase domain mutations after sequential inhibitor therapy define a refractory state

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Sequential use of increasingly potent ALK inhibitors has extended survival but selects for tumors bearing more than one substitution in the same kinase domain. We genotyped 232 post-progression specimens from patients treated with one to four inhibitors, using amplicon long-read sequencing to determine whether substitutions occupied the same allele. Single substitutions were found in 71 specimens and two or more in 38, of which 34 were phased to the same allele. The frequency of compound alleles rose with line of therapy, from 4 percent after one inhibitor to 35 percent after lorlatinib. G1202R plus L1198F and G1202R plus L1196M were the most common pairs. In isogenic systems, no approved inhibitor achieved an IC50 below achievable unbound concentrations against these pairs, whereas L1198F alone paradoxically restored crizotinib sensitivity. Progression confined to intracranial sites occurred in 44 percent of patients and was enriched among specimens lacking any kinase-domain substitution.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Each generation of ALK inhibitor was designed to overcome the substitutions selected by the previous one, and each has succeeded. The strategy assumes that resistant alleles arrive one at a time. Once two substitutions coexist on a single allele, the pocket is remodeled in ways that no ATP-competitive chemistry has yet accommodated, and the assumption fails. Whether such alleles are common enough to matter, and whether they arise preferentially under particular sequences of therapy, has not been established at scale because standard reporting collapses phase: two variants in one report may sit on one allele or on two, and only the former is refractory. We assembled post-progression specimens across lines of therapy and phased them to answer both questions.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Specimens were contributed by 18 centers from patients with rearranged disease who progressed on at least one inhibitor. DNA was amplified across the kinase domain in a single 3.1 kilobase amplicon and sequenced on a long-read platform to median 4,200-fold depth, with phase called when at least 50 reads spanned both positions. Isogenic Ba/F3 lines were generated for every allele or allele pair observed at least twice. IC50 values were determined across nine concentrations in triplicate and compared with published unbound steady-state concentrations for each drug. Sites of progression were abstracted from imaging reports by two reviewers. Association between line of therapy and compound allele frequency was tested by Cochran-Armitage trend test.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Of 232 specimens, 216 were evaluable. Kinase-domain substitutions were absent in 107, single in 71, and multiple in 38. Among the 38, phasing placed both substitutions on one allele in 34. Compound allele frequency rose from 3 of 74 after one inhibitor to 21 of 60 after lorlatinib, trend p less than 0.001. G1202R plus L1198F occurred in 11 specimens and G1202R plus L1196M in 8. In cellular assays, lorlatinib IC50 against G1202R alone was 34 nM but rose to 640 nM with L1198F; crizotinib IC50 against L1198F alone fell to 21 nM from 190 nM for parental fusion, confirming a resensitizing effect that disappeared in the compound context. Progression restricted to intracranial sites occurred in 95 patients, and among these only 21 had any kinase-domain substitution. Cells surviving prolonged exposure without any detectable substitution were recovered from three models and reverted to sensitivity on drug withdrawal.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Two conclusions follow. First, the refractory state produced by two substitutions on one allele is common enough after third-generation therapy to constitute a defined clinical problem, affecting roughly a third of biopsied patients, and it will not be solved by another increment in potency directed at the same pocket. Modalities that do not depend on pocket geometry are the logical next step. Second, phase must be reported. A specimen containing G1202R and L1198F implies an untreatable tumor if they are on one allele and a crizotinib-sensitive tumor if they are not, and current reports do not distinguish these. The observation that intracranial-only progression is largely unaccompanied by kinase-domain change points instead to inadequate drug concentration in that compartment, a pharmacologic rather than genetic problem. Reversible survival without any genetic change, described previously in EGFR-driven cultures, was reproduced here in fusion-driven models.

title: Mechanisms of progression on second-line osimertinib: paired tissue and plasma analysis of a randomized trial population

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: We analyzed paired pre-treatment and progression specimens from 205 patients who received osimertinib after progression on a first-generation EGFR inhibitor, combining tissue and blood profiling with central pathology review. The gatekeeper allele T790M, required for entry, was undetectable at progression in 108 of 191 evaluable patients, indicating loss of the population it marked. A tertiary substitution at codon 797 was present in 27 patients, 14 percent, and was accompanied by retained T790M in 24 of them. Copy gain at the MET locus occurred in 37 patients, 19 percent, ERBB2 amplification in 10, and oncogenic fusions in 8. Cell cycle gene alterations were present in 24. In 31 patients, 15 percent, no genomic mechanism was identified; among the 14 of these with adequate tissue, 4 showed morphologic change to a high-grade neuroendocrine phenotype with retention of the founding allele.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Osimertinib entered practice as a treatment for tumors selected by the presence of the gatekeeper allele, and understanding its failure requires knowing whether the gatekeeper-bearing population persists. Two broad patterns are possible. The tumor may remain dependent on the receptor and acquire a further change in the kinase domain, or it may reroute signaling through another receptor or downstream node, or abandon receptor dependence altogether. Distinguishing these requires paired sampling and, critically, tissue, because blood cannot report morphology and under-detects copy gain. Earlier reports have been small, single-institution, and mostly blood-only. We assembled the largest paired series to date from a randomized trial population with mandated progression sampling, allowing frequencies to be estimated with useful precision and allowing genomic and morphologic mechanisms to be counted in the same denominator.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Patients enrolled on a randomized trial of osimertinib versus platinum-pemetrexed after progression on a first-generation inhibitor contributed pre-treatment tissue, baseline plasma, and progression specimens. Tissue was profiled with a 468-gene hybrid capture panel; plasma with a 73-gene panel to a limit of detection of 0.1 percent. Copy gain was called at ratio above 2.0 in plasma and at copy number above 5 in tissue, with in situ hybridization confirmation where tissue permitted. All progression tissue underwent central pathology review with immunohistochemistry for synaptophysin, chromogranin, and TTF-1. Mechanisms were assigned hierarchically as on-target, bypass receptor, downstream, fusion, morphologic, or unidentified. Frequencies are reported with exact binomial confidence intervals; the association between mechanism and subsequent survival was explored with Cox models.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Of 205 patients, 191 had evaluable progression material, tissue in 96 and plasma in 178. T790M was undetectable at progression in 108 of 191, 57 percent. C797S was present in 27, always in patients with retained gatekeeper allele except in 3. MET copy gain was found in 37, with median ratio 2.9 in plasma and median copy number 9 in tissue; concordance between assays in the 62 patients with both was 82 percent. ERBB2 amplification occurred in 10, PIK3CA activating mutations in 9, KRAS mutations in 7, BRAF V600E in 3, and fusions involving RET, NTRK1, or FGFR3 in 8. CCNE1 amplification or CDKN2A loss was present in 24. No mechanism was identified in 31. Among 14 of those with reviewable tissue, 4 showed small cells with synaptophysin positivity and Ki-67 above 80 percent while retaining the founding EGFR allele. Median survival after progression was 11.7 months overall and 7.2 months in that morphologic subgroup.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Loss of the gatekeeper-marked population in more than half of patients indicates that osimertinib frequently fails not because the population it targets became resistant but because a different population, present all along and never dependent on that allele, expanded. This has a direct practical consequence: rebiopsy findings must be interpreted relative to the entering tumor, not in isolation. The tertiary substitution at codon 797, at 14 percent, is the most common single actionable finding and essentially always occurs in tumors that retained the gatekeeper, which constrains which combinations could work. That 15 percent of patients had no identifiable genomic mechanism, and that morphologic change was found in nearly a third of those with adequate tissue, argues strongly for tissue rather than blood at progression. Limitations include incomplete tissue availability and the fact that assay thresholds for copy gain were not harmonized between platforms.

title: Fragmented genomic escape from covalent KRAS G12C inhibition in lung adenocarcinoma

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Covalent inhibitors of KRAS G12C produce responses in roughly 40 percent of previously treated lung adenocarcinoma but median progression-free survival of only 6.5 months. We profiled progression specimens from 121 patients treated with sotorasib or adagrasib, using tissue where available and serial blood in all. A median of two independent alterations per patient was identified, and 33 patients, 27 percent, had three or more. Secondary substitutions in KRAS occurred in 21 patients, including Y96D, H95Q, and R68S, and a switch to a non-cysteine codon 12 allele in 6. MET copy gain occurred in 14, oncogenic fusions involving RET, ALK, BRAF, or FGFR3 in 13, activating alterations in NRAS, BRAF, MAP2K1 or PIK3CA in 29, and amplification of the wild-type KRAS allele in 9. Patients with three or more alterations had shorter subsequent survival, 4.9 versus 9.8 months.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: The clinical performance of the first covalent inhibitors of this target falls well short of what oncogene-directed therapy achieves in receptor-driven disease, and two explanations are usually offered. The pharmacologic one is that the drug traps only the inactive state, so any upstream input that reloads the protein with GTP restores signaling; the evolutionary one is that the tumors in question carry heavy mutational burdens from tobacco exposure and therefore harbor abundant standing variation. These are not mutually exclusive and make a shared prediction: escape should be diverse rather than convergent. Prior descriptions have been anecdotal, comprising case reports and small series in which multiple alterations were noted but not counted systematically. We set out to quantify the number of independent alterations per patient, because that number, more than the identity of any single event, determines whether sequential targeted salvage is a viable strategy.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Patients receiving sotorasib or adagrasib at four centers between 2019 and 2021 contributed blood at baseline, every 6 weeks, and at progression, with progression biopsy requested from all and obtained in 54. Blood was sequenced with a 129-gene panel to median unique depth 15,200-fold; tissue with a 468-gene panel plus RNA-based fusion capture. An alteration was counted as independent if it affected a distinct gene or a distinct codon and was not explicable as a passenger by variant allele fraction relative to the truncal driver. Alteration counts were compared across regimens with negative binomial regression adjusted for duration of therapy. Survival after progression was analyzed by Cox regression with alteration count as a categorical covariate.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Of 121 patients, 118 had evaluable progression material. Median number of independent alterations was 2, interquartile range 1 to 3, with 33 patients having three or more and 26 having none detected. Secondary substitutions within the target occurred in 21 patients, most commonly Y96D in 8; six patients acquired a codon 12 allele lacking the reactive cysteine, which cannot be engaged by either drug. Copy gain at the MET locus was found in 14, and in 5 of these it coexisted with a downstream activating mutation. Fusions were found in 13, of which 9 were detected only in tissue. Wild-type allele amplification occurred in 9. Duration of therapy correlated with alteration count, 0.31 additional alterations per 3 months. Median survival after progression was 9.8 months with fewer than three alterations and 4.9 months with three or more, hazard ratio 2.06.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Escape from this target is not a mechanism but a distribution. When the typical patient progresses with two and a quarter of patients with three or more independent alterations, sequential single-agent salvage directed at whichever alteration is reported first is unlikely to produce durable benefit, and trial designs premised on that approach should be reconsidered. The pattern contrasts sharply with receptor-driven disease, where a single dominant event is common. Two practical points follow. Tissue remains necessary, since a third of fusions were invisible in blood. And the reversible, non-genetic survival state described for EGFR-driven cultures, in which cells persist for weeks under continuous inhibition without acquiring any variant and revert to sensitivity on withdrawal, has a direct counterpart here: 26 patients progressed with no detectable alteration at all. Limitations include incomplete tissue sampling and heterogeneous prior therapy.

title: SHP2 inhibition suppresses adaptive receptor reactivation and deepens response to adagrasib in KRAS G12C lung adenocarcinoma

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Covalent KRAS G12C inhibitors trap the protein in its inactive state, but relief of ERK-dependent negative feedback restores upstream receptor signaling within hours and reloads newly synthesized protein with GTP, limiting depth of response before any mutation exists. We measured this rebound in 22 patients with biopsies at 6 and 48 hours after starting adagrasib. Phospho-ERK fell by a median of 71 percent at 6 hours and recovered to 46 percent of baseline by 48 hours, and the magnitude of recovery correlated inversely with subsequent tumor shrinkage, Spearman rho minus 0.58. Adding the SHP2 inhibitor TNO155 to adagrasib in 18 tumor models abolished the rebound, increased maximal regression from 38 to 74 percent, and extended median time to regrowth from 47 to 118 days. Escape from the paired regimen was less diverse, with a median of one alteration versus two.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: The gap between target engagement and clinical benefit for this class of drug is unusually wide. Occupancy of the reactive cysteine exceeds 90 percent at standard doses, yet responses are partial and brief. The explanation now favored is kinetic rather than genetic: the inhibitor can only capture protein that has cycled into the inactive conformation, and the cell responds to loss of ERK output by relieving feedback inhibition of receptor tyrosine kinases, which accelerates nucleotide exchange and returns protein to the active state faster than it can be trapped. If this account is correct, suppressing exchange should deepen response, and deeper early suppression should in turn leave a smaller and less varied population from which escape can be drawn. A survey of progression specimens reported that a median of two independent alterations coexisted per patient and that 27 percent harbored three or more, providing the comparator against which any reduction in escape diversity must be judged.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Patients starting adagrasib 600 mg twice daily on an institutional protocol consented to research biopsies at 6 and 48 hours. Phospho-ERK, phospho-S6, and phospho-AKT were quantified by immunofluorescence normalized to tumor cell nuclei, and GTP loading by RBD pulldown from flash-frozen tissue. Depth of response was the maximal percentage change in the sum of target lesion diameters. Eighteen tumor models from donors with G12C-mutant disease were treated with adagrasib alone, TNO155 alone, or both, at 10 animals per arm, dosed continuously to a regrowth threshold of twice nadir volume. Regrowth tumors underwent exome and fusion-capture sequencing. Alteration counts were compared by negative binomial regression.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Twenty-two patients provided paired biopsies. Median phospho-ERK suppression was 71 percent at 6 hours, with recovery to 46 percent of baseline at 48 hours; recovery varied widely, from 8 to 89 percent. Recovery correlated inversely with depth of response, rho minus 0.58. GTP loading recovered in parallel, from 22 percent of baseline at 6 hours to 68 percent at 48 hours. In models, adagrasib alone produced median maximal regression of 38 percent and median time to regrowth of 47 days. The pair produced 74 percent regression and 118 days, with phospho-ERK held below 20 percent of baseline at 48 hours. Combination toxicity was limited to reversible weight loss under 8 percent. Regrowth tumors from the combination arm carried a median of 1 alteration versus 2 from single-agent arms, and secondary target substitutions were less frequent, 2 of 14 versus 7 of 15.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Depth of early suppression is not merely a pharmacodynamic curiosity; it predicts both how much the tumor shrinks and how varied the eventual escape is. That the paired regimen produced fewer independent alterations at regrowth supports the evolutionary logic that a smaller surviving population has fewer opportunities to diversify, and it suggests that combination strategies should be evaluated on escape diversity as well as on progression-free survival. The 48-hour biopsy is the informative timepoint; 6-hour sampling shows only that the drug works. Clinically, the main obstacle is overlapping gastrointestinal and hepatic toxicity, which has limited dosing in early trials of this pair and which our models do not capture. Limitations include the modest number of patients with paired biopsies and the absence of a randomized clinical comparison.

title: Unbound partitioning of nine lung cancer kinase inhibitors across the neurovascular barrier and its transporter basis

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Reported tissue-to-plasma ratios for lung cancer kinase inhibitors span three orders of magnitude and are usually measured as total drug, which is uninterpretable for compounds that differ ten-fold in protein binding. We measured unbound partitioning for nine agents under identical conditions using microdialysis in tumor-bearing rats with equilibrium dialysis correction. Unbound ratios were 0.53 for lorlatinib, 0.39 for alectinib, 0.21 for osimertinib, 0.18 for entrectinib, 0.11 for brigatinib, 0.06 for adagrasib, 0.04 for sotorasib, 0.03 for crizotinib, and 0.02 for ceritinib. Total-drug ratios misranked five of nine agents. In Abcb1 and Abcg2 knockout animals, partitioning rose 12-fold for crizotinib and 1.3-fold for lorlatinib, indicating that efflux explains most of the variance. In stereotactic implantation models, unbound ratio predicted survival benefit better than potency, with rank correlation 0.81 versus 0.24.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Intracranial control has become the dominant determinant of outcome in oncogene-driven lung adenocarcinoma, because systemic disease is now controlled for years. Choosing among agents for that compartment currently relies on trial subsets of a few dozen patients and on partitioning values measured by different methods in different species. The measurement problem is not incidental. Only unbound drug crosses membranes and engages targets, and for highly bound compounds the unbound and total ratios differ by more than an order of magnitude, so comparisons based on total drug can invert the true ranking. A post-progression genotyping series is informative here: among patients whose disease progressed only in the neuraxis, kinase-domain substitutions were largely absent, implying that failure in that compartment reflects inadequate concentration rather than acquired insensitivity, and making the pharmacology decisive.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Male Sprague-Dawley rats bearing intracranial implants received each agent to steady state by twice-daily oral dosing for 5 days. Microdialysis probes were placed within tumor and in contralateral normal tissue, with sampling every 30 minutes for 8 hours and recovery determined by retrodialysis with a stable-label internal standard. Unbound fractions in plasma and tissue homogenate were determined by equilibrium dialysis at 37 degrees. Concentrations were measured by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry with a lower limit of quantitation of 0.1 ng/mL. Transporter contribution was assessed in Abcb1a/b and Abcg2 knockout rats and with elacridar co-administration. Efficacy used luciferase-labeled implants from four donors with 12 animals per arm and survival as the endpoint.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Unbound fractions in plasma ranged from 0.002 for lorlatinib to 0.11 for crizotinib. Unbound partitioning ratios in normal tissue were as reported in the abstract, with tumor tissue values 1.6 to 3.2-fold higher for every agent, reflecting local barrier disruption. Ranking agents by total-drug ratio changed the order for five of nine, most dramatically for lorlatinib, which ranked seventh by total drug and first by unbound measurement. Knockout of both transporters raised the crizotinib ratio from 0.03 to 0.36 and the alectinib ratio from 0.39 to 0.44, while lorlatinib changed from 0.53 to 0.69. Elacridar reproduced 70 percent of the knockout effect. In implantation models, median survival ranged from 28 to 74 days across agents, and rank correlation with unbound ratio was 0.81 compared with 0.24 for cellular potency against the driver.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Unbound measurement changes conclusions, and the field should stop reporting total-drug ratios for this class of compound. Efflux at the endothelium accounts for most of the between-agent variance, which means that partitioning is a predictable chemical property rather than an idiosyncratic one, and that transporter avoidance should be an explicit medicinal chemistry objective. Our efficacy data indicate that in this compartment exposure dominates potency: a less potent compound that reaches the target outperforms a more potent one that does not. Two limitations bear on interpretation. Tumor tissue partitioning exceeds normal tissue partitioning, so agents may control established lesions better than they prevent new ones in intact tissue. And rat transporter affinities differ modestly from human, so absolute values should be treated as ordinal.

title: Patritumab deruxtecan after progression on osimertinib: activity independent of the mechanism of progression

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: About half of patients progressing on osimertinib have no targetable alteration, and for them options are limited to platinum doublets. Patritumab deruxtecan directs a topoisomerase I payload to HER3, which is expressed on most EGFR-mutant tumors regardless of how they progressed. We report 145 patients treated at 5.6 mg/kg every three weeks after osimertinib and platinum chemotherapy. Confirmed objective response occurred in 44 patients, 30 percent, with median duration 6.4 months and median progression-free survival 5.5 months. Response rates were similar across mechanism categories: 31 percent with on-target substitutions, 27 percent with copy gain at the MET locus, 33 percent with no identified mechanism, and 3 of 11 with prior morphologic change. Membrane HER3 density, measured as receptors per cell, did not predict response, whereas SLFN11 expression above the median was associated with a response rate of 41 versus 19 percent.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: The post-osimertinib setting is the largest unmet need in this disease. Its defining feature is heterogeneity of mechanism: paired-biopsy series have shown that no single event accounts for more than a fifth of progressions and that a substantial fraction have no identifiable genomic explanation at all. A therapy addressed to a surface antigen rather than to a signaling dependency should in principle be indifferent to that heterogeneity. Whether it is, and what predicts benefit, are open questions. The prior experience with paired receptor blockade is instructive by contrast: adding a MET inhibitor to osimertinib produced responses in about half of patients with high-level copy gain, but only a minority of post-osimertinib tumors carry that alteration, so the approach is powerful and narrow. An antigen-directed payload could be broad, and our analysis was designed to test that claim directly.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Patients with EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma progressing after osimertinib and platinum chemotherapy received patritumab deruxtecan 5.6 mg/kg every 21 days. The primary endpoint was confirmed objective response by blinded independent review. All patients had progression material profiled centrally by tissue or blood sequencing, and mechanism was assigned by a pre-specified hierarchy. HER3 density was quantified on archival tissue by immunohistochemistry calibrated with cell lines of known receptor number and reported as receptors per cell. SLFN11 was measured by immunohistochemistry with H-score, dichotomized at the cohort median, specified before analysis. Interstitial lung disease was adjudicated by an independent committee.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Between 2020 and 2022, 145 patients were treated; median three prior lines, 38 percent with prior intracranial disease. Confirmed responses occurred in 44 patients, 30 percent, with median duration 6.4 months. Median progression-free survival was 5.5 months and median overall survival 12.9 months. Among 118 patients with an assigned mechanism, response rates were 31 percent for on-target, 27 percent for copy gain, 22 percent for downstream alterations, and 33 percent for unidentified. HER3 density spanned 4,000 to 190,000 receptors per cell and did not correlate with response, area under the curve 0.54. SLFN11 above median was associated with response in 41 versus 19 percent, odds ratio 2.9. Grade 3 or higher events occurred in 45 percent, chiefly thrombocytopenia and neutropenia; adjudicated interstitial lung disease occurred in 7 patients, 5 percent, with one death.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Activity is genuinely independent of how the tumor escaped, which is the central practical advantage of addressing a surface antigen rather than a signaling node, and it means the agent can be given without waiting for molecular results at progression. That antigen density does not predict response is consistent with experience across this drug class and suggests that internalization rate and payload sensitivity, rather than the number of available binding sites, are limiting; the SLFN11 association supports the latter. A 30 percent response rate with a median duration near six months is meaningful but not transformative, and the pulmonary toxicity signal requires vigilance. Limitations include the single-arm design, archival rather than contemporaneous tissue for antigen measurement, and the small number of patients with prior morphologic change.

title: Spatial immune contexture of EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma and the basis of checkpoint blockade failure

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Checkpoint blockade produces response rates below 10 percent in EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma despite these tumors containing lymphocytes. We applied imaging mass cytometry with a 36-marker panel to 204 specimens, 118 EGFR-mutant and 86 EGFR-wild-type, matched for stage and smoking history where possible. Total CD8 T-cell density did not differ, at 214 versus 246 cells per square millimeter, but their distribution did: in mutant tumors 79 percent of CD8 cells lay in stromal compartments more than 40 micrometers from the nearest tumor cell, versus 41 percent in wild-type. Tumor cell expression of HLA class I and B2M was reduced 2.6-fold, and antigen processing transcripts were coordinately lower. Macrophages in mutant tumors expressed higher CD163 and TGFB1. In an immunocompetent model, restoring class I expression by interferon-gamma pathway activation increased intratumoral CD8 infiltration 4.4-fold and conferred sensitivity to PD-1 blockade.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: The failure of checkpoint blockade in this population is one of the most reproducible negative results in thoracic oncology, and it is usually attributed to low mutational burden. That explanation is incomplete, since many of these tumors contain abundant lymphocytes and since burden correlates only loosely with benefit in other settings. Two alternative accounts predict different interventions: if T cells are present but physically excluded, the barrier is stromal and the remedy is to change trafficking; if the tumor cells cannot present antigen, the barrier is intrinsic and the remedy is to restore presentation. Bulk expression profiling cannot distinguish these because it averages over compartments. Single-cell profiling of residual disease during therapy showed that antigen presentation genes are coordinately suppressed in surviving cells, which suggested to us that the intrinsic account deserves direct spatial testing in treatment-naive tumors.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Resection and core biopsy specimens were retrieved from two institutional archives with annotation for driver genotype, stage, and smoking history. Imaging mass cytometry used a 36-marker panel including CD3, CD8, CD4, FOXP3, CD68, CD163, PD1, PDL1, HLA-ABC, B2M, TGFB1, and pan-cytokeratin, with ablation of four 1 square millimeter regions per specimen. Cells were segmented with a deep learning model and phenotyped by unsupervised clustering with manual annotation. Distance from each immune cell to the nearest cytokeratin-positive cell was computed. Mouse studies used an inducible EgfrL858R model on a C57BL/6 background; class I expression was raised by adenoviral delivery of a constitutively active STAT1 allele, with PD-1 blockade at 200 micrograms twice weekly and 12 animals per arm.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Of 204 specimens, 197 passed quality control. Total CD8 density did not differ between genotypes, p equals 0.38. Median distance from CD8 cells to the nearest tumor cell was 68 micrometers in mutant versus 27 in wild-type. Tumor cell HLA-ABC mean intensity was 2.6-fold lower in mutant tumors and B2M 2.2-fold lower, differences that persisted after adjustment for smoking history and stage. PD-L1 expression was low in both. CD163-high macrophages comprised 44 percent of myeloid cells in mutant versus 26 percent in wild-type, and TGFB1 signal was 1.9-fold higher. In the mouse model, STAT1 activation raised class I expression 5.1-fold and intratumoral CD8 density 4.4-fold; combined with PD-1 blockade it produced median survival of 74 days versus 39 with blockade alone and 41 with STAT1 activation alone.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Exclusion and presentation failure coexist in these tumors, but our intervention data indicate that presentation is the limiting step, since restoring class I expression alone was sufficient to bring T cells into tumor nests and to confer sensitivity to blockade. This reframes combination strategy: agents that increase infiltration without addressing presentation would not be expected to help, whereas interferon pathway agonists, epigenetic derepression of class I, or antigen-agnostic modalities should be prioritized. The finding also connects to what happens during targeted therapy, since presentation declines further at maximal response and does not recover at progression, suggesting that adding blockade after a targeted agent is the least favorable sequence. Whether the immunogenic cell death produced by delivering a topoisomerase I payload to a surface antigen can restore presentation and thereby licence a response is being tested in the same models. Limitations include archival material of variable fixation, the absence of matched on-treatment specimens, and a mouse model with low mutational burden.

title: A cereblon-recruiting bifunctional molecule eliminates EGFR triple mutants and compound ALK alleles

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Every inhibitor generation for EGFR and ALK has been answered by remodeling of the pocket it occupies. We describe WLT-233, a bifunctional molecule linking a reversible EGFR-binding element to a cereblon ligand, which removes receptor protein rather than blocking its catalytic activity. WLT-233 reduced receptor protein by 94 percent within 4 hours in cells bearing L858R with T790M and C797S, with DC50 of 14 nM and sustained suppression of ERK signaling for 48 hours after washout. Activity was independent of whether the tertiary substitution lay on the same allele as the gatekeeper, which determines whether inhibitor combinations retain activity. A companion molecule built on an ALK-binding element removed fusion protein bearing G1202R plus L1198F and G1202R plus L1196M and inhibited growth of models bearing those alleles. Resistance selections yielded CRBN frameshift alterations in 7 of 9 recovered clones.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Pocket-directed chemistry has a structural ceiling. When a tumor acquires two substitutions within one kinase domain, or a tertiary substitution on the same allele as the gatekeeper, the geometry that any ATP-competitive compound must accommodate becomes incompatible with adequate potency and selectivity. Phasing work has shown that allelic configuration determines whether inhibitor pairs retain activity, and that the untreatable configuration predominates in previously treated patients. A modality that eliminates the protein does not depend on that geometry, needs only transient binding to form a ternary complex, and acts catalytically. Whether this promise survives contact with the alleles that defeated inhibitors, and whether it introduces a new and easily acquired escape route through loss of the recruited ligase, are the two questions this work addresses.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Bifunctional molecules were assembled from a reversible aminopyrimidine EGFR binder or a lorlatinib-derived ALK binder connected through polyethylene glycol and alkyl linkers of 8 to 16 atoms to pomalidomide. Ternary complex formation was measured by time-resolved fluorescence energy transfer with cooperativity reported as alpha. Protein loss was quantified by capillary immunoassay and confirmed by targeted mass spectrometry, with DC50 and maximal loss fitted from eight concentrations. Allelic panels comprised nine EGFR and six ALK configurations in isogenic Ba/F3 lines plus twelve models grown from patient tumors, including two with ROS1 fusions carrying G2032R. Resistance selections used 10 to the eighth cells at 3 and 10 times DC50, with recovered clones sequenced across CRBN, CUL4A, DDB1, and RBX1.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: WLT-233 formed a cooperative ternary complex with alpha of 4.2 and achieved DC50 of 14 nM with 94 percent maximal protein loss against the triple mutant. Signaling suppression outlasted compound washout by 48 hours, whereas an equipotent inhibitor control recovered within 4 hours. Growth inhibition GI50 was 22 nM against the cis configuration and 19 nM against trans, a difference within assay variability, in contrast to inhibitor pairs which differed more than 80-fold between configurations. The ALK-directed molecule achieved DC50 of 31 and 44 nM against the two compound alleles and produced regression of 51 percent in a model bearing G1202R plus L1198F. Cereblon protein was detectable in all twelve tumor models at levels above the threshold required for activity. Resistance selections at 3 times DC50 yielded outgrowth in 9 of 24 replicates, and 7 of 9 clones carried frameshift alterations in CRBN.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Removing the protein is genuinely indifferent to the pocket alterations that defeat inhibitors, and the comparison of allelic configurations makes that concrete: a difference of nearly two orders of magnitude for inhibitor pairs collapses to nothing for the bifunctional molecule. The trade-off is a new dependency. Loss of the recruited ligase arose readily in selection and would be invisible to standard genomic reporting, which does not include CRBN. Ligase-agnostic strategies, or molecules that recruit an alternative ligase, deserve parallel development, and clinical trials of this modality should sequence the ligase machinery at progression. The structure-guided insertion-selective inhibitors developed for other EGFR alleles remain complementary, since brain exposure for bifunctional molecules of this size is likely to be limited. Limitations include the absence of in vivo pharmacokinetic optimization and the reliance on immunodeficient hosts.

title: Racial, insurance, and geographic differences in broad molecular profiling and receipt of matched therapy in advanced lung adenocarcinoma

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Matched targeted therapy improves survival only if the alteration is identified and the drug is started. We studied 11,438 patients with newly diagnosed advanced non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer in a linked electronic health record and claims resource between 2018 and 2022. Broad profiling within 8 weeks of diagnosis was completed for 7,104 patients, 62 percent. Among 2,619 patients with an actionable result, 2,048 started matched therapy within 12 weeks, 78 percent. Completion of profiling was lower for Black than for White patients, 54 versus 64 percent, adjusted odds ratio 0.71, and lower in practices outside metropolitan areas, adjusted odds ratio 0.62. Once an actionable result existed, initiation of matched therapy differed less by race but strongly by time to result: each additional week of turnaround was associated with a 9 percent lower likelihood of starting the matched agent, largely because chemotherapy had already begun.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Two decades of molecular therapeutics in lung adenocarcinoma have produced agents that extend survival by years in selected patients. The benefit is conditional on a sequence of steps, each of which can fail: a sufficient specimen must be obtained, a broad panel must be ordered, the result must return before a treatment decision is made, and the matched agent must be accessible. Prior work has typically reported a single completion figure, which obscures where the failure occurs and therefore what would fix it. Community-practice outcome studies have shown that patients who do receive a matched agent achieve survival close to trial estimates, which implies that the loss is concentrated in the cascade rather than in the drugs. We therefore decomposed the pathway into an ordering step and an initiation step and examined determinants of each separately.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: The cohort comprised adults with newly diagnosed stage IIIB to IV non-squamous disease in a de-identified linked resource covering 280 practices. Broad profiling was defined as a panel assessing at least 50 genes, from tissue or blood, resulted within 8 weeks of diagnosis. Actionable results were those matched to an approved agent. The two outcomes were profiling completion and initiation of matched therapy within 12 weeks, modeled by multivariable logistic regression with practice-level random effects and adjustment for age, sex, race, ethnicity, insurance, rurality, stage, performance status, and practice volume. Turnaround time was modeled as a continuous covariate. A 1,200-patient chart validation subsample confirmed algorithmic ascertainment with positive predictive value 0.94.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Of 11,438 patients, 7,104 completed profiling within 8 weeks. Completion was 64 percent among White, 54 percent among Black, and 61 percent among Hispanic patients; adjusted odds ratios versus White were 0.71 and 0.88. Medicaid coverage was associated with an adjusted odds ratio of 0.66 and non-metropolitan practice location 0.62. Insufficient tissue was documented in 18 percent of patients who did not complete profiling. Among 2,619 patients with an actionable result, 78 percent started matched therapy within 12 weeks; adjusted racial differences were attenuated, odds ratio 0.91 for Black versus White. Median turnaround was 16 days, and each additional week was associated with an odds ratio of 0.91 for initiation. Among patients whose result returned after 4 weeks, 42 percent had already started chemotherapy.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: The cascade fails at two points for different reasons. Whether a panel is ordered and completed depends on specimen adequacy and on practice setting, and it differs by race and insurance in a way that adjustment for measured covariates does not remove. Whether the matched agent is started depends chiefly on whether the result arrives before the first treatment decision. These call for different remedies: reflex ordering at pathology sign-out and a blood sample drawn at the first oncology visit address the first, while neither addresses the second unless turnaround is also shortened. Community-practice outcome data showing median overall survival close to 26 months among patients who received first-line third-generation therapy underscore what is lost when the cascade breaks. Limitations include residual confounding, incomplete capture of care outside the network, and inability to observe patient preference.

title: Effectiveness and tolerability of first-line osimertinib in community oncology practice

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Trial estimates for first-line osimertinib derive from selected populations treated at academic centers. We assembled 1,842 patients with advanced EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma who started first-line osimertinib between 2018 and 2021 in community practices. Median age was 71, 22 percent had ECOG performance status 2 or worse, and 31 percent had intracranial disease at baseline, compared with 41 percent and 5 percent and 19 percent in the registration trial. Median time to treatment discontinuation was 16.2 months and median overall survival 25.6 months. Dose reductions occurred in 14 percent and permanent discontinuation for adverse events in 9 percent. Patients with performance status 2 or worse had median overall survival of 14.1 months versus 29.4 months for status 0 to 1. Only 46 percent underwent any molecular testing at progression, and 21 percent received a subsequent systemic therapy within 90 days of stopping.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Registration trials establish efficacy in patients selected for organ function, performance status, and willingness to attend frequent visits. Whether the same benefit is realized in ordinary practice is a separate empirical question, and one that matters for the counseling of individual patients and for health system planning. The relevant comparison is not simply median survival but the distribution of the population: community cohorts are older, more often have poor performance status, and more often have untreated intracranial disease. A further question specific to this drug concerns what happens afterwards. Progression on this agent is heterogeneous and a rational next step usually requires knowing the mechanism, so the frequency with which testing is actually performed at progression bears directly on whether the mechanistic literature can be applied at all.

sections.name: Methods
sections.text: Patients were identified from a de-identified electronic health record resource covering 280 predominantly community practices. Eligibility required advanced or metastatic non-squamous disease, a documented sensitizing EGFR alteration, and initiation of osimertinib as first systemic therapy for advanced disease between 2018 and 2021. Time to treatment discontinuation was defined from first dose to last administration plus one dosing interval or death, and overall survival from first dose, with censoring at last structured activity. Performance status was taken from the value recorded closest to initiation. Adverse events were captured from structured toxicity fields and from dose modification records rather than from prospective grading. Survival was estimated by Kaplan-Meier and compared with Cox models adjusted for age, sex, performance status, mutation type, intracranial disease, and practice volume. Molecular testing after progression was ascertained from linked laboratory reports within 60 days of discontinuation.

sections.name: Results
sections.text: Of 1,842 patients, 1,187 had exon 19 deletions and 583 L858R. Median follow-up was 24 months. Median time to treatment discontinuation was 16.2 months, 95 percent confidence interval 15.1 to 17.4, and median overall survival 25.6 months, 95 percent confidence interval 23.8 to 27.9. Twelve-month survival was 76 percent. Among 405 patients with performance status 2 or worse, median overall survival was 14.1 months versus 29.4 months for 1,437 with status 0 to 1, adjusted hazard ratio 1.92. Patients with baseline intracranial disease had median survival of 21.8 months. Dose reduction occurred in 258 patients, most often for rash, diarrhea, or paronychia, and 166 discontinued for adverse events. Of 1,204 patients who progressed, 553 had any molecular testing within 60 days, and among those an actionable finding was reported in 148. Testing after progression was less frequent among patients older than 75, those with Medicaid coverage, and those treated outside metropolitan areas, at 34, 39, and 41 percent respectively.

sections.name: Discussion
sections.text: Overall survival in ordinary practice is roughly six months shorter than in the registration trial, and essentially all of the difference is attributable to performance status and to age rather than to any difference in how the drug behaves. That is reassuring for the drug and sobering for extrapolation: patients with performance status 2 should be counseled with the 14-month figure rather than the trial figure. The more consequential finding is that fewer than half of patients underwent testing at progression. An adjuvant trial in resected disease reported a disease-free survival hazard ratio of 0.20 and moved the drug into earlier settings, which will enlarge the population reaching progression; if the mechanistic workup is not performed, none of the salvage strategies developed over the past decade can be applied. Limitations include unmeasured confounding and reliance on structured fields for performance status.

title: Osimertinib after complete resection of stage IB to IIIA EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma: disease-free survival and postoperative molecular residual disease

sections.name: Abstract
sections.text: Recurrence after complete surgical removal of EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma remains common despite platinum-based chemotherapy. In this double-blind study, 682 patients with completely removed stage IB to IIIA disease were assigned 1:1 to osimertinib 80 mg daily or placebo for three years. Disease-free survival strongly favored osimertinib, hazard ratio 0.20 with 95 percent confidence interval 0.14 to 0.30; two-year disease-free survival was 89 versus 53 percent in stage II to IIIA. Central nervous system disease-free survival also favored treatment, hazard ratio 0.18. In a pre-specified substudy of 288 patients, tumor DNA was detectable in blood at 4 weeks after surgery in 61 patients, and detection was associated with recurrence risk, hazard ratio 5.4, independent of stage. Among patients with detectable postoperative DNA, treatment reduced recurrence more markedly, hazard ratio 0.11, than among those without.

sections.name: Introduction
sections.text: Surgery cures a minority of patients with stage II and III lung adenocarcinoma, and adjuvant platinum chemotherapy adds roughly 5 percentage points to five-year survival.
